detail.title: TimesL: A Generic Hierarchical Framework for Mitigating Spectral Bias and Gradient Starvation in Time Series Forecasting
detail.abstract: Time series forecasting plays a pivotal role in applications ranging from finance to climate science; however, its efficacy is frequently hampered by the complex, multi-scale characteristics of real-world data. A critical bottleneck in current deep forecasting models is their inherent spectral bias towards high-energy dominant patterns. Driven by standard end-to-end optimization, models greedily fit large-amplitude trends while starving subtle, high-frequency predictive details of learning gradients. To address this asymmetric optimization dynamic, we propose TimesL, a generic hierarchical framework engineered to decouple and balance multi-scale feature extraction. By synergizing a novel decomposition module with a progressive, layer-wise training strategy (TimesL-Train), our approach explicitly forces the network to capture secondary granularities without them being overshadowed by dominant components. Extensive experiments across five mainstream forecasting tasks demonstrate that TimesL effectively mitigates this representation suppression, achieving state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance while exhibiting robust generalization on diverse empirical datasets.

title: A Novel Hybrid Implementation of Memristive Neuron Networks
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Novel Hybrid Implementation of Memristive Neuron Networks
detail.abstract: Memristive neural networks (MNNs) are neuromorphic circuits that provide an effective framework for investigating the complex behaviors exhibited by biological neural systems. In general, physical validation of MNN dynamics relies on purely analog or digital circuits. Here, we introduce a hybrid analog–digital implementation of two coupled Hindmarsh–Rose (HR) neurons interconnected through a second-order memristor. The proposed hybrid architecture integrates analog neuron circuits to capture continuous-time neuronal dynamics, with digital memristor implementation on a digital signal processor (DSP) board, enabling flexible tuning and manipulation of memristor parameters. The dynamics of the coupled systems are studied using bifurcation and Lyapunov exponent diagrams, revealing chaotic behavior, transient chaos, coexisting attractors, and phase synchronization. Digital processing causes some delay, but the experimental attractors from the hybrid platform closely match the numerical simulations. This confirms the main dynamical features across the tested parameter range.

title: Statistical Discrimination and Labor Force Participation
affiliations: United States Naval Academy

detail.title: Statistical Discrimination and Labor Force Participation
detail.abstract: This paper explores the role of productivity-based statistical discrimination (PBSD) in black-white employment-related outcome gaps using a structural model. Given a worker's race and a noisy signal of their productivity, employers rely on race-specific averages to inform their expectations. Such discrimination results in worse employment prospects for black workers. I discipline the model using 1997 NLSY data on less-educated young prime-aged white and black males and a novel calibration strategy. My results suggest PBSD plays at most a limited role in non-participation, unemployment, and hiring gaps, while productivity differences are likely much more important.

title: Orchestrating Federated Tabular Synthesis at Scale with Fault-Tolerant Pipeline Execution
affiliations: Kyungpook National University

detail.title: Orchestrating Federated Tabular Synthesis at Scale with Fault-Tolerant Pipeline Execution
detail.abstract: Cross-silo tabular datasets support many machine learning applications, but regulations and governance often forbid centralizing raw records. Federated synthesis of synthetic tables under differential privacy (DP) offers a practical alternative; however, data partitioning inflates variance of local statistics and per-site DP noise accumulates at the aggregator, producing a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) bottleneck that harms fidelity. This paper introduces \system{}, a fault-tolerant pipeline that orchestrates workload-guided DP synthesis across many parties. Instead of federating high-dimensional neural weights, the system estimates and securely aggregates low-dimensional noisy histogram marginals and trains a generative model on the aggregate, which limits sensitivity growth with model size under DP. The design integrates adaptive communication with error-feedback quantization, hierarchical aggregation for coordinator scalability, checkpointing with cache-based recovery when parties disconnect, and incremental updates when workloads evolve. On eight public tabular benchmarks compared against five federated and centralized baselines, marginal-based \system{} improves workload accuracy relative to weight-based federated generators and federated diffusion training, while adaptive coding reduces communication volume compared with na\"ive transfers. Results consistently indicate that cross-party distribution heterogeneity is the dominant residual error source compared with privacy noise alone, informing privacy budget choices in heterogeneous consortia.

title: TADLE: A Temporal Attention-based Dual-Stream LSTM Heterogeneous Ensemble for Electricity Price Trend Forecasting
affiliations: Jilin University and Zhejiang University

detail.title: TADLE: A Temporal Attention-based Dual-Stream LSTM Heterogeneous Ensemble for Electricity Price Trend Forecasting
detail.abstract: Electricity price trend forecasting is critical for optimizing power market trading strategies, mitigating dispatch risks, and enhancing energy allocation efficiency. This paper proposes an Temporal Attention-based Dual-Stream Heterogeneous Ensemble (TADLE) model, which synergistically integrates the sequential modeling capability of a dual-stream LSTM with the nonlinear fitting strength of LightGBM through an MLP-based meta-learner. To address the inherent class imbalance in price movement prediction, a BalancedFocalLoss function is incorporated to improve training stability and minority-class recall. Systematic experiments on the Australian NSW-VIC electricity market dataset demonstrate that TADLE achieves state-of-the-art performance, attaining an F1-score of 0.8545 and an AUC of 0.9477. Compared to the strongest baseline (LightGBM), the proposed model improves F1-score by 0.4%, AUC by 0.3%, and reduces the business-oriented CostScore by 1.6%. Furthermore, TADLE exhibits remarkable robustness and data efficiency: under a 20% feature missing scenario, the F1-score remains 0.7454, and with only 25% of the training data, it still reaches 0.7974. These results establish TADLE as a high-precision, resilient, and cost-effective solution for electricity price trend forecasting.

title: Modular Distributed Method for Integrating Demand Response in Optimization using Demand Shift Potential Curves
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, DBFZ German Biomass Research Center gGmbH, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Modular Distributed Method for Integrating Demand Response in Optimization using Demand Shift Potential Curves
detail.abstract: The increasing share of volatile renewable energy sources requires the development of innovative strategies to address the temporal and spatial mismatches between energy production and consumption. On the production side, predictive, optimization-based methods can be employed to effectively use available flexibility. On the consumption side, Demand Side Management (DSM) offers a promising solution by enabling load shifting, resulting in peak shaving and valley filling. However, integrating DSM into optimization frameworks remains challenging due to the computational complexity growing with the number of consumers. Scalable approaches using price-based mechanisms, on the other hand, often lead to rebound effects or load synchronization, undermining overall system efficiency.This paper introduces a novel distributed method for integrating DSM in the form of Demand Response into highlevel optimization. The objective of this approach is to facilitate an optimal interaction of all controllable generators, storages, and consumers using demand shift potential curves. The method employs a hybrid, non-market-based approach that models flexible demand as a virtual storage system. By using precomputed shift potential curves and coordinating demand adjustments through distributed agents and a central coordinator, the method enables scalable, temporally aware optimization without explicitly modeling each consumer in the optimization problem. This architecture effectively mitigates dynamic inefficiencies associated with traditional DSM methods.The method was validated using a district heating network simulation with 18 heterogeneous residential consumers. Results demonstrate that the proposed method successfully reduced morning peak loads and improved base-load boiler utilization by reshaping demand profiles. Despite minor deviations between optimized and realized shift curves, the method maintained the contractually guaranteed conditions and consumer comfort.

title: Predicting ship energy requirements through a diversified learning framework and multi-dimensional feature integration
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Predicting ship energy requirements through a diversified learning framework and multi-dimensional feature integration
detail.abstract: To make shipping more environmentally friendly, ships must lower their energy use and emissions. Accurate forecasting of ship fuel consumption—also known as vessel fuel consumption (VFC)—is key. Fusing high-complexity, varied sensor streams (such as speed, weather, and engine sensors) into unified diagnostic architectures remains challenging. In this study, we introduce a multi-level framework for estimating fuel usage through diverse-scale data blending. Central to our approach is a dual-layered attention-based merging system called TSAFNet (Two-Stage Attention Fusion Network). This system uses importance-weighted data refining to enhance feature representation (how input data characteristics are captured) and allows adaptive integration across branches (model components processing different data types). We tested TSAFNet with a monthly dataset from fishing boats. The experimental results show that TSAFNet outperforms ten other models. Our model reduces the average absolute deviation (a measure of prediction error) by 42.0% and the quadratic mean deviation by 25.7% compared to the strongest baseline. Ablation studies—which test the impact of removing model parts—and cross-vessel tests with data from different ships show that the model is robust and may suit many situations. This research allows ships to operate more efficiently by making more precise VFC predictions and supports the goal of decarbonising the maritime industry.

title: What Leaders Get Wrong About Emotional Intelligence How to Recognize and Correct the Misperceptions That Undermine Leadership Development and Effectiveness
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: What Leaders Get Wrong About Emotional Intelligence How to Recognize and Correct the Misperceptions That Undermine Leadership Development and Effectiveness
detail.abstract: Organizations spend billions annually on emotional intelligence assessments, coaching, and leadership development, and most of it fails to change behavior. This article argues the core reason is not resistance or lack of resources: it is systematic misperception. While prior research has clarified what emotional intelligence is and dispelled common misconceptions about the construct itself, far less attention has been paid to how leaders interpret their own EQ feedback in practice. Leaders correctly identify their EQ profiles but assign the wrong meaning to what they observe, directing their development efforts in precisely the wrong direction. Drawing on more than 20 years of executive coaching practice and approximately 1,500 EQ-i 2.0 development engagements, this article catalogs 15 recurring misperceptions, one aligned with each of the EQ-i 2.0's 15 competency dimensions, and pairs each with a concrete, immediately applicable corrective tool and a direct prescription for action. A full misperception framework, 90-day development plan, and diagnostic map are included for leaders, coaches, and HR professionals.

title: Structural Modeling of Annual Hourly Load in China A Unified Framework for Coupled Dynamics and Irregular Holiday Effects
affiliations: The University of Hong Kong, Tsinghua Sichuan Energy Internet Research Institute, The University of Hong Kong and The University of Hong Kong

detail.title: Structural Modeling of Annual Hourly Load in China A Unified Framework for Coupled Dynamics and Irregular Holiday Effects
detail.abstract: Effective planning and operation in China’s evolving power system require a structural understanding and modeling of the annual hourly (8760-hour) load profile. This task is exceptionally challenging due to two primary complexities: First, the intricate coupling of multi-factor dynamics and the profound, irregular effects of China’s unique holiday system. Second, the structural uncertainty that reflects the complex temporal dependencies in the load’s randomness. To address these challenges, we propose a unified framework centered on the generalized additive model (GAM) to model annual hourly load. Our approach moves beyond black-box methods by structurally decomposing the load to explicitly model its underlying drivers, featuring novel components that capture the year-by-year load evolution and the finegrained, rule-based effects of China’s irregular holidays. Building on this, we design a two-stage method to quantify predictive uncertainty and generate a set of temporally coherent load scenarios by explicitly modeling the residual correlation structure. Evaluated on 12 years of real-world data from Guangdong, China, our framework has been proven to deliver superior accuracy in deterministic forecasts, higher quality in probabilistic forecasts, and generate scenarios that are both probabilistically consistent and realistic, providing a powerful and interpretable tool for modern power system decision-making, enabling tangible economic benefits and improved risk management in critical applications such as annual electricity procurement.

title: New theories for new realities? A systematic review of Outward Foreign Direct Investment from Emerging Economies
affiliations: University of Regensburg

detail.title: New theories for new realities? A systematic review of Outward Foreign Direct Investment from Emerging Economies
detail.abstract: The scholarly debate on whether established internationalization theories adequately explain the behaviour of emerging economy multinational corporations (EMNCs) has persisted for two decades. This systematic literature review analyses this debate by conducting a theory-fit analysis of EMNC outward foreign direct investment (OFDI) research, evaluating not only which theoretical frameworks are applied but whether they hold up when empirically tested. Drawing on 83 peer-reviewed articles from leading international business journals, the study examines theoretical foundations, empirical testing outcomes, and the role of home and host country contexts across diverse emerging economy settings.Bibliometric and content analyses reveal that traditional frameworks, notably Internalization Theory, the OLI paradigm, and the Uppsala model, remain the most widely applied and demonstrate the strongest explanatory performance when augmented with institutional logic. Theories developed specifically for EMNCs, including the linkage, leverage, learning model and Springboard perspective, are less frequently tested and were classified as empirically inapplicable in every direct test identified. Of all frameworks subjected to empirical testing, only 53% proved fully applicable, with applicability consistently higher when institutional factors were structurally integrated rather than treated as moderating controls.These findings contribute to ongoing theoretical debate about EMNC internationalization: the empirical record favours contextual extension of established frameworks over adoption of EMNC-specific alternatives. More fundamentally, the results reframe institutional context not as a moderating variable but as a boundary condition that determines the applicability of international business theory itself, a distinction with significant implications for how the field should prioritise future theoretical development.

title: Collaborative Planning Framework for Heavy-Duty Truck Electrification: Corridor-Port Integrated Energy Systems
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Hohai University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Nanyang Technological University (NTU) - School of Civil and Environmental Engineering and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Collaborative Planning Framework for Heavy-Duty Truck Electrification: Corridor-Port Integrated Energy Systems
detail.abstract: Deep decarbonisation of heavy-duty truck freight is essential for global carbon neutrality. As vital intermodal hubs, ports can support the development of green freight corridors. However, existing research on port integrated energy systems primarily focuses on internal logistics and vessels, neglecting corridor- port energy-demand coupling. To bridge this gap, we propose a ”Corridor-Port Integrated Energy System” (C-PIES) framework and develop a two-stage distributionally robust optimisation model to address uncertainties in renewable energy generation and freight traffic flow. Using high-frequency GPS trajectory data, ambiguity sets are constructed to support robust scheduling of port renewable energy for corridor traffic-driven loads. A case study of Quanzhou Port shows that C-PIES enables source-load-storage coordination through battery swapping stations reducing system cost by 42.89% and carbon emissions by 50.2% compared with the isolated mode. The results demonstrate the potential of ports as regional energy hubs for low-carbon freight corridors.

title: Monetary Tightening and Financial Stability in Oil-dependent Emerging Markets: Evidence of Nonlinear Policy Trade-offs
affiliations: Central Bank of Nigeria, Central Bank of Nigeria and

detail.title: Monetary Tightening and Financial Stability in Oil-dependent Emerging Markets: Evidence of Nonlinear Policy Trade-offs
detail.abstract: This study investigates the non-linear trade-off between taming inflation and financial system stability in oil-dependent emerging markets, focusing on Nigeria (2015-2025). Using a Threshold Vector Autoregressive (TVAR) framework, we identify a structural tipping point at an Open Repo Rate (OPR) of 6.64 per cent. (OPR was used as a high-frequency proxy for the monetary policy stance). This threshold bifurcates the economy into "Normal" and "Aggressive" policy regimes. Our findings reveal that Nigeria operated within the Aggressive regime for 83.7 per cent of the sample. In this state, monetary policy acts as a stress multiplier; while high rates intended to defend the currency may curb inflation, they trigger persistent, self-reinforcing systemic stress. Generalised Impulse Response Functions (GIRFs) further identify a "Vulnerability Feedback Loop," where aggressive tightening renders the financial system hypersensitive to exchange rate shocks and external volatility. The study concludes that exceeding the threshold creates a dilemma where the pursuit of price stability may generate unintended pressures on financial stability. We recommend that central banks in resource-rich nations institutionalise regime-specific macroprudential buffers and decouple exchange rate defense from interest rate hikes once rates surpass identified thresholds to prevent systemic banking crises.

title: Options Volume as Noise: Evidence from Three Decades of Earnings Announcements
affiliations: Rutgers Business School - Rutgers University

detail.title: Options Volume as Noise: Evidence from Three Decades of Earnings Announcements
detail.abstract: We examine whether pre-announcement options activity predicts earnings surprises and returns using 69,094 firm-quarters from 1996–2024. Contrary to the “smart money” hypothesis, high option-to-stock volume (O/S) predicts lower returns: a quintile hedge portfolio earns −39 basis points in the announcement window (t = −3.79) and −118 basis points in post-earnings drift (t = −4.60). These robust patterns suggest options volume reflects hedging and uninformed speculation, rather than informed trading. Only the put–call ratio robustly predicts standardized unexpected earnings (t = −2.90), distinguishing the information content of option prices versus volume. Crucially, we document a structural break coinciding with the late-2019 zero-commission shift: the O/S coefficient predicting CAR[0, +1] flips from negative (t = −2.04) in 1996–2005 to positive (t = +2.77) in 2020–2024. This implies the retail trading surge fundamentally altered the information content of aggregate option volume. Our findings inform literature on options informativeness, anomaly decay, and retail participation.

title: Economics and Religious Identity
affiliations: Department of Economics, University of Oxford

detail.title: Economics and Religious Identity
detail.abstract: Religion is a cultural universal. Sacred stories, places, objects, and ritual practices are found in every known human society, past and present. Complex societies allow for religious diversity through separation of the sacred and secular. Despite adhering to different religions, people interact in the secular sphere using shared conventions, laws, and moral codes. Religious identity consists of a belief system and set of markers that tells us who adheres to which religious beliefs and practices. In this chapter, I explain why distinct religious identities persist despite intensive mixing in the secular sphere (e.g. education, employment). First, religious identity can help solve collective action problems and enable high-functioning communities. Second, religious identity can signal underlying preferences and structure interactions in heterogenous societies. Third, religious identity can help solve crises of meaning and belonging created by societal atomization. Finally, I discuss the conditions under which religious identification can become pathological and fuel conflict.

title: Monetary Policy under Fiscal Shadows: Evidence from ECOWAS
affiliations: Central Bank of Nigeria and Nile University of Nigeria

detail.title: Monetary Policy under Fiscal Shadows: Evidence from ECOWAS
detail.abstract: This study examines fiscal dominance in ECOWAS, focusing on WAEMU and WAMZ in the context of the proposed Eco currency. Using a dynamic panel ARDL-PMG framework and data from 2000-2023, the paper assesses whether fiscal imbalances influence inflation, constrain monetary policy, and interact with central bank independence. The results provide evidence of fiscal dominance across the region, with stronger effects in WAMZ, where monetary policy appears more constrained and exchange rate pass-through is significant. In contrast, WAEMU's common monetary framework partially mitigates these pressures. Central bank independence is found to reduce inflation, though its effectiveness varies across institutional settings. The findings raise concerns about the sustainability of convergence and the readiness of ECOWAS for monetary union, highlighting the need for stronger fiscal discipline, institutional credibility, and policy coordination.

title: Evaluating the Success of the Bank of Spain's Measures in the Restructuring of the Banking System after the Great Recession
affiliations: University of Malaga, University of Malaga and University of Malaga

detail.title: Evaluating the Success of the Bank of Spain's Measures in the Restructuring of the Banking System after the Great Recession
detail.abstract: This research analyses and compares the characteristics of traditional banks with those resulting from the transformation or merger of savings banks, with the objective of evaluating the effectiveness of the restructuring measures of the Spanish banking system ten years after the 2008 crisis. Using a non-parametric Mann-Whitney Z-test and a factor analysis using principal components, the results indicate that banks derived from savings banks are larger and more digitised than traditional banks. However, traditional banks remain more efficient and perform better. In practice, understanding the effects of banking system restructuring after the crisis provides valuable information for central banks assessing the impact of similar measures.

title: Institutions, Geography, and Intra-African Trade: Evidence from Long-Run Gravity Models
affiliations: Sultan Qaboos University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Sultan Qaboos University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Institutions, Geography, and Intra-African Trade: Evidence from Long-Run Gravity Models
detail.abstract: This paper examines how multilateral and regional trade institutions relate to intra-African trade over the long run. Using bilateral trade data for African countries from 1962 to 2020, the analysis combines descriptive evidence, network analysis, and multiple gravity model specifications. Intra-African trade remains sparse and highly concentrated, with many zero trade flows and a small number of dominant exporters. Geographic distance and contiguity consistently explain trade patterns across all models. Joint membership in regional economic communities and the World Trade Organization is positively associated with trade in parsimonious specifications, but these effects weaken in highly saturated fixed-effects models. This sensitivity suggests that institutional indicators primarily capture long-run structural integration rather than short-term policy effects. The findings support AfCFTA’s role as a gradual, cumulative framework for continental trade integration.

title: Unifying Information Theory and Causal Inference: A Variational Framework for Interpretable Deep Learning with Continual Learning Capability
affiliations: Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics, AECC Hunan Aviation Powerplant Research Institute, Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Nanjing Forestry University and Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

detail.title: Unifying Information Theory and Causal Inference: A Variational Framework for Interpretable Deep Learning with Continual Learning Capability
detail.abstract: Abstract:  To address the lack of interpretability in deep neural networks and the issue of catastrophic forgetting in continual learning, this paper establishes a unified theoretical framework for interpretable deep learning grounded in information theory, causal inference, and variational inference. Building on the variational information bottleneck (VIB) principle, we first propose a location-aware ConvFormer architecture, which achieves the theoretically optimal trade-off between compressibility and predictability in representation learning by minimizing the upper bound of mutual information while maximizing mutual information metrics. Moving to causal modeling, we formalize counterfactual paths in the deep feature space within Pearl’s structural causal model (SCM) framework, deriving causal effects via do-calculus to establish robust causal chains from features to predictions. Leveraging graph theory and random walk theory, we further construct a dynamic knowledge graph, with rigorous proofs for the convergence of knowledge propagation and the uniqueness of PageRank centrality. Beyond these components, interpretability optimization is modeled as a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP), where the approximate optimality of the proposed policy is established through Lagrangian duality theory. Finally, under the Bayesian paradigm, we design a multi-source information fusion mechanism that enables uncertainty quantification via variational posterior inference. Theoretical analysis rigorously verifies the strong convergence of the optimization algorithm, and the Pareto frontier between interpretability metrics and model capacity is shown to be approximable via convex optimization. Systematic experiments on the Split MNIST, Split CIFAR-10, and industrial equipment fault datasets provide empirical validation of our theoretical predictions.

title: Research Trends on Income Instability and Financial Behaviour among Gig Workers: A Bibliometric Review
affiliations: Lovely Professional University

detail.title: Research Trends on Income Instability and Financial Behaviour among Gig Workers: A Bibliometric Review
detail.abstract: The gig economy has fundamentally changed the identity of employment relations as well, as unstable, platform-centric labour arrangements are replacing permanent, wage-based contracts. Even though gig work is associated with freedom and increased access to the market, it is characterised by income instability, earnings insecurity, and reduced access to formal social safety nets. These circumstances have a significant impact on gig workers' monetary behaviour, including risk management, borrowing, saving, and consumption smoothing. Although there has been an increasing academic interest, the current studies are still scattered across the fields, theoretical frames, and geographical settings. The present research is a systematic bibliometric evaluation aimed at tracing the intellectual framework, the research directions, and thematic development related to income instability and financial behaviour of gig workers. The analysis conducted with the help of 5,461 peer-reviewed scholarly journal articles published between 2008 and 2025, accessed via the Dimensions.ai database, uses descriptive and relationship bibliometrics methods, such as the analysis of publication trends, citation, comprehension of the co-authorship networks, and mapping the co-occurrence of keywords. Results show that academic output increased significantly after 2018 due to the rise in the spread of digital labour platforms around the world and the increased awareness of financial precarity. The burgeoning groups include algorithmic governance, financial inclusion, and social protection, and the leading topics include income volatility, financial stress, debt dependence, and labour regulation. However, the empirical evidence on the developing economies, especially India, is very limited. The research confirms the conceptual gaps, the relevant contributors and journals, synthesises the scattered literature, and suggests the areas of future research to inform the policy and financial inclusion efforts on behalf of gig workers.

title: How Can Enhancing the Level of Financial Literacy Among Financial Consumers Contribute to Financial Stability: Aligning Two Critical Policy Objectives
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: How Can Enhancing the Level of Financial Literacy Among Financial Consumers Contribute to Financial Stability: Aligning Two Critical Policy Objectives
detail.abstract: Several studies show that the level of financial literacy is alarmingly low in many jurisdictions. This was argued as a contributing factor to the Global Financial Crisis and made recovery from the GFC more difficult. In parallel, the surprise of and the disruptions from the GFC surfaced the need to manage systemic risks, elevating this as a separate, though nuanced, objective. We ask how financial literacy initiatives align into a macroprudential framework. We do this by constructing a portfolio choice model that depends on the consumer’s appreciation of his own level of financial literacy. Although consumers each decide what is best for themselves, they are interlinked because the assets across individual portfolios are naturally substitutes or complements. In addition, aggregating the choices among individual consumers causes externalities. We define society’s well-being by accounting for such externalities, which is dependent on the coverage and quality of information, as well as the capability of the market to hedge against risks. The target of the authorities i.e., achieving a well-functioning and resilient market, is defined by different combinations between information and market structure. We show that risks at the level of society may still arise even if consumers are well-informed and maximize their own utility. Furthermore, we show that financial literacy initiatives need to be designed differently under different combinations of information and market structure. This informs the macroprudential authority on the information and market structure issues that it needs to address, while providing the financial literacy authority a clear guideline on how it should structure the contents of its education initiatives.

title: Dwelling Type, Time-to-Build, and Housing Price Volatility: Theory and Evidence from OECD Countries
affiliations: Chonnam National University

detail.title: Dwelling Type, Time-to-Build, and Housing Price Volatility: Theory and Evidence from OECD Countries
detail.abstract: This paper investigates how the share of apartments in housing stock a ects monetary policy transmission to house prices. We develop a two-asset HANK model with loan-to-value (LTV) constraints and type-dependent time-to-build (TTB) frictions. Due to longer construction lags and greater supply inelasticity, our model predicts that apartment-heavy markets exhibit nearly twice the price volatility and six times the wealth inequality impact following a monetary shock. Using panel local projections, we nd that real house prices in high-apartment economies show a distinct "overshooting-and-reversal" pattern dropping faster and more steeply at medium horizons (quarters 4~12) compared to house-dominated markets. This result is robust to alternative speci cations and cuto s. Notably, the e ect is asymmetric across contractionary and expansionary shocks, directly supporting the time-to-build mechanism.

title: mHC-DEIM: Object Detection for Shelf Scenes under Dense Arrangement, Multi-Angle Inclination and Low-Illumination
affiliations: Harbin University of Science and Technology, Harbin University of Science and Technology and Harbin University of Science and Technology

detail.title: mHC-DEIM: Object Detection for Shelf Scenes under Dense Arrangement, Multi-Angle Inclination and Low-Illumination
detail.abstract: Dense object detection is essential for intelligent retail systems and automated inventory management, as it substantially improves operational efficiency. However, several challenges remain: feature confusion caused by densely packed arrangements leads to missed detections of small objects. Multi-view, oblique perspectives produce redundant and overlapping bounding boxes due to limited geometric constraints. Additionally, low signal-to-noise ratios under low-light conditions result in frequent false positives within the background. This research introduces mHC-DEIM, a model based on the Detection Transformer with Improved Matching (DEIM) architecture, which integrates Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) into the Transformer component of the DEIM framework. By projecting residual maps onto the Birkhoff polyhedron and coupling this with residual flow expansion, mHC preserves the identity mapping property while enhancing expressive capacity. Increasing the channel width improves object detection performance in high-density scenarios, whereas the mapping constraints aid in stabilizing results across multi-view oblique scenes and during training. To mitigate false high-frequency background detections caused by low signal-to-noise ratios in low-light environments, this architecture utilizes pinwheel-shaped convolutions (PSConv) within the backbone network HGNetv2 to expand the receptive field and augment the signal-to-noise ratio under low illumination. Extensive experiments on the SKU110K dataset demonstrate that mHC-DEIM markedly enhances both average accuracy and inference speed relative to real-time detectors such as DEIM, D-Fine, and DEIMv2, thereby effectively advancing object detection in dense, multi-view, and low-illumination scenarios.

title: Closed-Form Thresholds in CARA Optimal Stopping via the Lambert W Function
affiliations: Università della Svizzera italiana

detail.title: Closed-Form Thresholds in CARA Optimal Stopping via the Lambert W Function
detail.abstract: When a CARA agent faces a perpetual stopping problem under incomplete markets with an affine terminal payoff, the free-boundary condition reduces to an implicit equation that Henderson (2007) identifies but leaves without a closed form. The main observation of this paper is that once a reference cost c > 0 is present in the payoff, the equation reduces to the Lambert W equation we^w = z with z in (-1/e, 0), and that among the two real solutions, only the W_{-1} branch satisfies the maintained admissibility restriction that net proceeds be positive at the stopping boundary. We prove this Branch Selection Theorem and show that for c = 0 the canonical equation has no strictly positive admissible solution. A companion Amplification Theorem establishes that the derivative dV*/dc exceeds 1/alpha >= 1 throughout the admissible region, with an explicit closed-form formula for the slope and a Cauchy-Schwarz argument for the variance bound. Three illustrative applications – irreversible investment under incomplete markets, secondary liquidation of a private-equity stake, and a junior creditor’s claim-exercise problem – show how the canonical parameter assignment carries distinct economic content across investment, finance, and credit settings.

title: Death Cost of Migration in Nepal
affiliations: Tribhuvan University and Tribhuvan University - Tri-Chandra Multiple Campus

detail.title: Death Cost of Migration in Nepal
detail.abstract: Nepal is a country where labour migration is not just an economic trend but a social reality. With limited job opportunities at home and families depending on remittances, hundreds of thousands of Nepalese leave annually for employment abroadespecially to Gulf countries and Malaysia. While remittances help the nation's economy, the human cost of migrationparticularly deaths of migrant workershas become a pressing crisis with deep emotional, financial, and social consequences. For many families in Nepal, migration is a necessary but risky path that can bring both financial benefits and heart breaking losses. While remittances support the nation's economy, the death cost of migrationhuman, emotional, social, and financialremains profound. Better policies, protections, and opportunities are essential to ensure that Nepali migrants can work abroad without risking their lives.

title: Inside the Loop: Decision Speed, Attrition, and Asymmetric Conflict
affiliations: Southern Illinois University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Inside the Loop: Decision Speed, Attrition, and Asymmetric Conflict
detail.abstract: Why does the weaker side sometimes win a war of attrition against a vastly richer opponent? Contest theory has studied resource asymmetry in rich detail but has always assumed that both players observe, decide, and act on the same schedule. This paper breaks that symmetry by introducing decision-cycle speed as a new dimension of asymmetry. One player re-optimizes every period; the other is locked into a committed posture for multiple periods. When the environment shifts between decisions, the locked-in player fights at discounted effectiveness, burning resources at full rate for diminished returns. The paper derives a closed-form threshold for the critical tempo gap above which the faster but poorer player wins; this threshold is the Markov perfect equilibrium outcome, not a myopic approximation. An existence condition draws the boundary: if the environment is too stable relative to the resource gap, no finite tempo advantage suffices. The threshold is robust to forward-looking effort optimization, which shifts it by less than two percent. The model provides the first economic formalization of Boyd's OODA (Observe-Orient-Decide-Act) loop. Applications to the Iran-U.S. confrontation and the Russia-Ukraine war illustrate the predictions. A multi-front extension yields closed-form retreat and proliferation bounds.

title: National Security Threats in West Africa: Causes, Impacts, and Strategic Responses
affiliations: Maharaja Ranjit Singh Punjab Technical University (MRSPTU)

detail.title: National Security Threats in West Africa: Causes, Impacts, and Strategic Responses

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no personal, financial, or professional conflicts of interest that could have influenced the research or the preparation of this manuscript. This study was conducted independently and received no external funding.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is based entirely on the analysis of publicly available literature, policy reports, and secondary data sources. No human participants, personal data, or confidential information were involved in the research. Therefore, ethical approval was not required for this study.

detail.abstract:
West Africa has increasingly become a focal point of global security concerns due to the proliferation of complex and interrelated threats that challenge national stability and regional integration. Over the past two decades, the region has experienced a significant rise in violent extremism, political instability, transnational organized crime, and maritime insecurity. Countries such as Nigeria, Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger, and Guinea have faced persistent security crises that undermine governance structures, economic development, and human security. Violent extremist organizations including Boko Haram and the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) have expanded their activities across borders, transforming local conflicts into regional security threats [1][2]. At the same time, recurring military coups in several West African countries have weakened democratic institutions and disrupted governance systems [3]. Transnational organized crime networks and maritime piracy have further complicated the security landscape by exploiting weak border controls and fragile institutions [4][5]. 

This research examines the major national security threats facing West Africa and analyzes their root causes, socioeconomic impacts, and strategic responses adopted by governments and regional organizations. The study employs a qualitative research methodology using secondary data drawn from academic literature, policy reports, and security assessments. Findings indicate that insecurity in West Africa is driven by a combination of structural and political factors including poverty, youth unemployment, environmental pressures, weak governance, and porous borders [6][7]. These factors create conditions that allow extremist groups and criminal networks to flourish. The study concludes that addressing national security threats in West Africa requires comprehensive strategies that combine military interventions with socioeconomic development, institutional reforms, and strengthened regional cooperation.

title: LM-HTR: Learnable Masking Attention for Historical Text Recognition
affiliations: , Sharda University and

detail.title: LM-HTR: Learnable Masking Attention for Historical Text Recognition
detail.abstract: Handwritten text recognition (HTR) is critical for the digital preservation and subsequent retrieval of historical manuscripts. Despite this, the diverse range of handwriting styles, spacing, and degradation of documents due to factors like fading, ink bleed-through, and background noise remain issues with existing systems. While transformer-based recognizers provide strong global contextual modeling, dense self-attention may capture the noisy background rather than informative handwriting structures. We propose a transformer-based line-level HTR framework that integrates spatially selective attention mechanisms to improve robustness in a training-from-scratch setting without synthetic data augmentation or external language models. The framework enhances discriminative feature learning through deformable attention, which sparsely samples content-adaptive spatial locations, and learnable masking attention, which emphasizes informative handwriting regions while suppressing background interference. Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) loss is used to train the model end-to-end. Experiments on the READ2016, LAM, and IAM benchmarks demonstrate improvements over existing transformer-based HTR approaches, particularly on degraded manuscripts. The results indicate that spatially selective attention provides an effective design strategy for improving robustness and accuracy in archival handwritten text recognition.https://anonymous.4open.science/r/HTR-VT-8943/README.md

title: Getting to Equal: Persistence of Entry Salary Disadvantage on the Gender Pay Gap
affiliations: Independent, Asian Development Bank and

detail.title: Getting to Equal: Persistence of Entry Salary Disadvantage on the Gender Pay Gap

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Two of the authors (Molina-Lapid and Zveglich) were staff of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) at the time of writing. The ADB department in charge of human resources—which requested the original study that forms the foundation for this paper and provided the anonymized staff data—gave the authors autonomy to analyze the data, interpret the results, and publish their findings. An advisory committee led by the ADB Chief Economist, which included noted external academics and ADB subject experts, provided technical feedback at various stages of the original study’s development.

detail.abstract: This study traces gender salary gap trends among internationally recruited staff at a multinational development institution over 2000-2022. Although the unadjusted gap narrowed substantially, progress was neither linear nor complete. Using panel data on individual staff and Blinder-Oaxaca decomposition methods, we find that gender differences in entry salaries persisted throughout employees' tenure, outweighing any catch-up from subsequent salary growth and promotions. Entry salary disparities account for approximately one-third of the gender gap in current salaries-an effect concentrated at the lower end of the salary distribution and negligible among higher-paid staff.

title: The Price of Representation: Congressional Redistricting and Housing Markets

detail.title: The Price of Representation: Congressional Redistricting and Housing Markets
detail.abstract: This paper provides the first causal evidence that congressional redistricting affects residential property values and housing market activity, establishing political representation as a capitalized amenity in housing markets. Exploiting the 2022 redistricting in Harris County, Texas as a quasi-natural experiment, I compare 1.09 million properties whose congressional district assignment changed to those whose assignment remained stable, using annual data from 2017-2025. Average redistricting effects are modest and imprecise, but meaningful heterogeneity emerges along two dimensions. Properties experiencing a partisan flip in district control suffer a 7.9% decline in market values and a 0.35 percentage point increase in deed transfer probability, consistent with political misalignment imposing disutility on residents. Properties moved to more electorally competitive districts experience a 7.4% increase in market values and higher transaction rates, suggesting that electoral accountability is valued as a local amenity. These effects are persistent across alternative estimators designed to account for pre-existing neighborhood trends, alternative sample definitions, and controls for gentrification dynamics. The findings demonstrate that political geography shapes urban economic geography through non-pecuniary channels, independent of schools, taxes, and local services, and that gerrymandering imposes real economic costs on households by destroying competitive representation and disrupting partisan alignment.

title: More income, less crime Evidence from Italy
affiliations: Bank of Italy

detail.title: More income, less crime Evidence from Italy
detail.abstract: I study whether minimum income affects property crime and consumption, exploiting the introduction and subsequent withdrawal of Reddito di Cittadinanza (RdC), the Italian minimum income scheme introduced in 2019. Using administrative data and spatial variation in the intensity of program participation across regions and provinces, I estimate the aggregate effect of RdC on crime and household expenditures. I find that RdC reduced thefts by about 20% (on an annual basis) between 2019 and 2022, while it had no effect in 2023, when eligibility conditions were tightened. Over the same period, household consumption increased by approximately 2.5%, driven entirely by non-food expenditures. The effects are stronger in Southern Italy, where there were more program beneficiaries, and are mitigated by local employment conditions. Violent crimes are unaffected. A welfare analysis based on the Marginal Value of Public Funds yields an MVPF of 1.3, indicating that the policy repaid its fiscal cost. These results provide evidence that minimum income can substitute for illegal income sources and generate net social benefits, even over a relatively short policy horizon.

title: Public Sector Wage Differentials in a Federal System: Disentangling Institutions
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Lucerne

detail.title: Public Sector Wage Differentials in a Federal System: Disentangling Institutions
detail.abstract: We investigate wage differentials between the public and private sector in Switzerland, distinguishing between federal, cantonal, and municipal administrations as well as public enterprises. Applying state-of-the-art matching methods in combination with quantile regression, we find that the wage premium decreases with wage levels, with the highest premium at the federal administration and the lowest at the municipal level. Public enterprises pay higher wages than the private sector across the entire wage distribution but lower wages than the federal administration. Our findings highlight the importance of considering institutional heterogeneity when analyzing public sector wages.

title: Is India the “New China” In U.S. Foreign Policy?
affiliations: Seattle University Law School

detail.title: Is India the “New China” In U.S. Foreign Policy?
detail.abstract: As China and the United States become estranged, or “decoupled,” this essay explores the United States’ relationship with India considering this trend. The U.S.-India foreign relations are stronger today than they have been in India’s 75-year history as an independent nation.2 To understand why this is the case, we must examine both the U.S. and Indian foreign policy perspectives. The United States’ interest in India has grown in part due to the United States’ own changes in domestic policy and motivations to counter China. It is only in the more recently that India has been open to a stronger partnership with the United States due largely to political and economic changes in the country.

title: Risk-Aware Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning and Blockchain Enforcement for Peer-to-Peer Trading Market and Demand Response in Residential Energy Communities
affiliations: Polytechnic of Milan, University of Canterbury, Chitkara University, University of Canterbury, , Khalifa University and The University of Manchester

detail.title: Risk-Aware Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning and Blockchain Enforcement for Peer-to-Peer Trading Market and Demand Response in Residential Energy Communities
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a risk and uncertainty-aware energy management and market framework for residential energy communities (REC) operating in electric distribution networks under high-frequency uncertainty. The REC model captures aggregated household demand, photovoltaic generation, battery energy storage, electric vehicles with controlled charging and vehicle-to-grid capability, and flexible electrical appliances coordinated through demand response (DR). To operationalize DR while preserving privacy and accountability, we integrate a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) decision layer with a blockchain-enforced peer-to-peer (P2P) markets layer. Each community agent observes local electrical states, market prices, and reputation signals, and selects dispatch and bidding actions that jointly maximize social welfare and DR delivery while explicitly penalizing tail-risk and infeasibility. Smart-contract commitments, settlement, penalties, and reputation updates provide verifiable compliance and deter strategic manipulation without exposing household-level profiles. Extensive simulations on three benchmark systems, including IEEE 33-bus, Caracas 141-bus, and IEEE 342-bus networks, demonstrate scalable performance across small, real-data-driven, and large-scale settings. Under nominal operation, the proposed method achieves welfare of 4,280/16,450/58,900 $/day with DR fulfillment of 96.1/95.0/93.6% and low downside exposure, and it consistently outperforms multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO) and centralized soft actor critic (SAC). Under hybrid cyber-physical disturbance, the framework exhibits controlled degradation, sustaining higher welfare and lower CVaR than baselines while maintaining zero hard constraint violations.

title: Social Networks and Corporate Environmental Policy
affiliations: , University of Glasgow and University of Edinburgh Business School

detail.title: Social Networks and Corporate Environmental Policy
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether and how directors' social networks influence firms' environmental policies. We show that the similarity in environmental policies between firms increases with the number of shared director connections. We highlight that punishment plays a critical role in this process: firms mimic poor environmental practices of peers if no significant punishment occurs but improve their policies when peers face severe consequences. We use directors' deaths to address endogeneity concerns, finding that policy similarity decreases when a connecting director passes away.

title: Soil, Soul, and Solvency: How Glacial Endowments Shaped Religion, Finance, and Social Capital in America

detail.title: Soil, Soul, and Solvency: How Glacial Endowments Shaped Religion, Finance, and Social Capital in America
detail.abstract: Why are some societies more devout than others, and how do historical environments shape modern financial culture? While classic secularization theories predicted a linear decline of religion with industrialization, the global landscape of belief is far more complex (Iyer, 2016). This paper argues that both secularization and financial development in the United States can be traced to deep geological time. I propose a novel causal chain: Pleistocene glaciation left exceptionally fertile soil, which reduced economic risk and income volatility faced by agrarian communities. This environmental stability weakened the demand for all forms of insurance-both religious (social insurance) and financial (debt as consumption smoothing)-leading to lower religious participation and reduced mortgage debt. Using historical glacial coverage as an instrument for agricultural land quality, I find large parallel effects: a 10 percentage point increase in prime farmland density decreases the 1890 religious participation rate by 3.4 percentage points and the mortgage rate by 3.7 percentage points. These effects persist for over a century, shaping modern social capital and economic prosperity. This demonstrates that deep environmental endowments can shape the foundations of a society's cultural, religious, and financial life through a unified risk-management framework.

title: Event-Driven Econometric Forecasting: A Unified Framework for Financial Prediction and Systemic Risk Assessment

detail.title: Event-Driven Econometric Forecasting: A Unified Framework for Financial Prediction and Systemic Risk Assessment
detail.abstract: This paper introduces an event-driven econometric framework that unifies financial forecasting, volatility dynamics, and systemic risk assessment through a Gaussian news-impact structure. The model integrates four core determinants of asset-price movements—market capitalization, volatility, trading volume, and event shocks—into a transparent and computationally efficient predictive system. Event impacts are modeled using a Gaussian decay function that captures both the magnitude and temporal structure of news-driven responses, while volume acts as an amplification mechanism reflecting market microstructure dynamics. In addition to forecasting, the framework proposes a novel collapse-risk index that links leverage exposure to downside volatility, offering an early-warning indicator of corporate and sovereign distress. Empirical evaluations across equities, currencies, inflation, and labor markets show that the model consistently outperforms ARIMA, GARCH, VAR/VECM, and LSTM benchmarks in directional accuracy, RMSE, and MAPE. Statistical validation using Diebold–Mariano tests confirms significant predictive gains. By combining econometric interpretability with event-driven responsiveness, the proposed framework bridges traditional time-series models and modern data-driven approaches, providing a unified tool for forecasting, stability analysis, and policy evaluation

title: A Comparative Analysis of Hybrid Finance Models for SMEs Financing in Emerging and Developed Economies: Nigeria and Poland as Examples

detail.abstract: Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) face a persistent financing gap globally, estimated at significant portions of GDP in emerging markets like Nigeria, while facing different structural barriers in developed economies like Poland. Decentralized Finance (DeFi) offers theoretical solutions through peer-to-peer lending and tokenized assets, yet pure DeFi adoption remains low among SMEs due to regulatory uncertainty, technical complexity, and volatility. This paper employs Institutional Theory (North, 1990) and Ozili's (2023) tripartite framework of regulation, infrastructure, and capacity to compare the Nigerian and Polish contexts. Drawing on a synthesis of recent literature (2018-2026), the study argues that "pure" DeFi is ill-suited for immediate SME adoption in either context. Instead, a "Hybrid Finance" model where regulated fintech intermediaries bridge traditional banking and blockchain protocols offers the most viable pathway. The analysis highlights Nigeria's reactive regulatory stance (e.g., the 2021 ban and subsequent lifting) versus Poland's adaptive integration within the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) framework. The paper concludes that institutional embedding, rather than technological disruption alone, is critical for closing the SME financing gap.

title: Axiomatic Admissibility and Evaluator-Level Screening
affiliations: Merope

detail.title: Axiomatic Admissibility and Evaluator-Level Screening
detail.abstract: This paper studies evaluator-level admissibility in panel decision-making. The mechanism of interest does not modify scores candidate by candidate, but determines whether an evaluator's entire report profile retains influence in aggregation. An axiomatic characterisation is developed using requirements of profile-level screening, screening-aggregation separation, exchangeability, affine invariance, quasi-concavity, continuity, a local full-admissibility core, and extreme non-admissibility. The main representation result shows that every mechanism in this class admits a pointwise scale-free representation in terms of a deviation index and an opponent-profile-specific retention map. A second result shows that extreme nonadmissibility is equivalent to eventual loss of influence for every non-consensus opponent profile. The former is stated in the original multidimensional report space, whereas the latter is a tail condition on the represented retention map. Under an additional benchmarksufficiency condition, the profile-indexed family collapses to a single common retention function, recovering the structure of operational centre-based threshold rules. Under monotone aggregation, eventual loss of influence bounds best replies pointwise and eliminates unbounded escalation. Evaluator-level admissibility is thereby identified as a distinct governance layer, separate from score-level correction and compatible with unchanged aggregation of retained reports.

title: Ill-Posed Reporting Games Under Monotone Aggregation
affiliations: Merope

detail.title: Ill-Posed Reporting Games Under Monotone Aggregation
detail.abstract: This paper studies reporting games induced by monotone aggregation on unbounded strategy spaces. It shows that when evaluators retain influence at arbitrarily extreme reports, the induced game may be ill posed: best-response correspondences can be empty, and equilibrium analysis becomes vacuous. This pathology does not arise from informational frictions, equilibrium multiplicity, or strategic complexity, but from a structural interaction between monotonicity, unbounded reporting domains, bounded attainable payoffs, and persistent influence. The main contribution is to identify eventual loss of influence as a sufficient structural condition that regularises such games. When sufficiently extreme reports lead to exclusion with probability approaching one, those reports become strictly dominated by safer alternatives. This dominance relation endogenously confines strategically relevant best responses to a bounded subset of the action space, even though the original reporting domain remains unbounded. Once best responses are non-empty and pointwise bounded, standard equilibrium-existence arguments become available as a corollary rather than as a primitive assumption. The regularisation mechanism operates independently of equilibrium reasoning, belief formation, or truth-telling assumptions. By focusing on well-posedness rather than equilibrium selection, the paper clarifies a basic limitation of monotone aggregation in strategic reporting environments and identifies a structural mechanism through which such games can be made amenable to standard game-theoretic analysis.

title: Nigeria's Petroleum Market, 2023 to 2026: Price Ceiling Removal, Supply Distortions, Refinery Market Structure, Strategic Pricing Dynamics, Externalities, and Production Efficiency

detail.title: Nigeria's Petroleum Market, 2023 to 2026: Price Ceiling Removal, Supply Distortions, Refinery Market Structure, Strategic Pricing Dynamics, Externalities, and Production Efficiency

detail.abstract: On May 29, 2023, Nigeria abolished its long-standing fuel subsidy, ending nearly five decades of administered price controls on Premium Motor Spirit. Within hours, the pump price rose from N198 to N540 per liter, and by October 2024, it had reached N1,030 per liter, a cumulative increase of 421 percent. This paper applies eight microeconomic models to analyze Nigeria's petroleum market across a thirty-four-month window from May 2023 through March 2026. The analysis establishes that the annual welfare loss attributable to the price ceiling was approximately N1.456 trillion, equivalent to 2.7 percent of GDP. Consumers absorbed 76.2 percent of the total price increase, consistent with the estimated price elasticity of supply and demand in the Nigerian fuel market. At the regulated ceiling, model-calibrated supply fell to 11.1 million liters per day against demand of 55 million liters per day, generating a daily shortage of 43.9 million liters and a black-market price of approximately N772 per liter, consistent with observed informal market prices of N600 to N800 per liter. A fully scaled direct household cash transfer program would have delivered greater distributional efficiency at no additional fiscal cost to the government. The entry of the Dangote Petroleum Refinery into commercial PMS production in September 2024 transformed the downstream market from a de facto import monopoly into an asymmetric Cournot duopoly. Sequential price reductions by Dangote drove the pump price to approximately N699 per liter by December 2025. As of January 2026, Dangote supplied 40.1 million liters per day, representing 61.78 percent of total national PMS supply. An exogenous crude price shock driven by Middle East conflict pushed Brent crude above $80 per barrel on March 2, 2026, and to approximately $102 per barrel by March 9, 2026, triggering a sequence of upward gantry price adjustments by Dangote, reaching N1,175 per liter on March 9 before a partial reduction to N1,075 on March 10. Pump prices across major branded stations in Lagos and Abuja ranged from N1,025 to N1,300 per liter as of March 12, 2026. Aggregate macroeconomic indicators registered measurable improvement: the consolidated fiscal deficit narrowed from 4.8 to 4.1 percent of GDP between 2023 and 2024, while gross international reserves rose to $40 billion. Household welfare deteriorated sharply across the lower income distribution. By 2024, an estimated 47 percent of Nigerians lived below the poverty line, and 25.1 million people experienced acute food insecurity during the October through December harvest season. The cash transfer program designed to protect vulnerable households reached only 5.5 million of the 15 million target households. In aggregate, the reform achieved its stated fiscal objectives but fell substantially short of its social protection goals.

title: Electricity Load-Shedding, Threshold Effects, and Cross-Border Macroeconomic Spillovers in Sub-Saharan Africa

detail.abstract: This paper constructs the Electricity Load-Shedding Intensity Index (ELSII) for 40 sub-Saharan African countries from 2000 to 2024 and estimates its macroeconomic consequences using panel threshold regression and cross-sectional spatial analysis. The ELSII is derived through principal component analysis of electricity non-access rates and transmission and distribution losses from the WDI Indicators, providing a continuous, time-varying measure of electricity unreliability with broad panel coverage. Baseline fixed effects estimation with Driscoll-Kraay standard errors yields a statistically significant negative effect on log real GDP per capita (β =-0.013, p = 0.039). Panel threshold regression confirms a pronounced nonlinear relationship: below the estimated critical threshold of γ̂ =-0.661, the macroeconomic penalty per unit of load-shedding is approximately 4.7 times larger (β₁ =-0.065, p < 0.001) than in the above-threshold, higher insecurity regime (β₂ =-0.014, p = 0.047), with the bootstrap linearity test rejected at the 1% level. This finding demonstrates that economies transitioning from adequate supply toward deteriorating grid reliability suffer far greater output losses than those already adapted to chronic electricity scarcity. A cross-sectional Spatial Durbin Model based on country time-means identifies a statistically significant spatial lag (W × ELSII = 0.502, p = 0.032), consistent with investment and trade diversion toward relatively electricity-stable neighbors during regional electricity crises. Moran's I statistics confirm positive spatial clustering in macroeconomic residuals across 9 of 13 sampled biennial years. The findings carry direct implications for ECOWAS, SAPP, and EAPP regional energy cooperation, showing that nationally framed energy policy systematically underprices the cross-border externalities of grid failure.

title: Investor ESG Sentiment and Stock Returns: The Mediating Role of Media Coverage
