detail.abstract: This study investigates how ESG-related media coverage influences stock returns, comparing investor responses during the stable market of 2019 and the COVID-19 crisis in 2020. Using data from S&P 1500 firms and MarketPsych, we find that ESG media attention significantly shapes investor behavior, with stronger effects during periods of uncertainty. Negative ESG coverage-especially in headlines-correlates with lower returns during crises, reflecting heightened investor risk aversion. In contrast, detailed news articles positively influence returns under normal conditions, while social media shows minimal impact. ESG controversies also have a more persistent negative effect during crises. These findings highlight the importance of media narratives in ESG analysis and investment strategy, particularly when traditional financial signals are less reliable.

title: Unlocking the land-sparing potential of wake steering: Complementary roles of nested and sequential co-design in multi-objective wind farm optimization
affiliations: Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU), affiliation not provided to SSRN, The University of Hong Kong, Shanghai University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU) and Hong Kong Polytechnic University - Renewable Energy Research Group

detail.title: Unlocking the land-sparing potential of wake steering: Complementary roles of nested and sequential co-design in multi-objective wind farm optimization
detail.abstract: The massive global expansion of wind energy demands extensive land use, increasingly creating conflicts with biodiversity conservation, agriculture, and local communities. Traditional wind farm layout optimization primarily focuses on maximizing power output while overlooking land-use efficiency. To address this tension, this study proposes a multi-objective co-design framework that integrates wake steering to concurrently optimize annual energy production (AEP) and capacity density, implemented via nested and sequential optimization workflows. The framework utilizes the NSGA-II algorithm coupled with the Generalized Serial-Refine (GSR) method, an advanced deterministic solver that optimizes yaw angles for wake steering. One-outer-iteration tests demonstrate that GSR matches the solution quality of the global-search Genetic Algorithm while requiring 3.4 times less computational cost, thereby making nested co-design tractable. Moreover, the sequential and nested workflows follow distinct evolutionary trajectories, leading to qualitatively different Pareto frontiers. By decoupling layout from control, the sequential approach converges to static‑optimum layouts at significantly lower computational cost, making it a pragmatic choice for engineering deployment. Nonetheless, the nested strategy remains indispensable for uniquely identifying control-complementary layouts in highly constrained sites. Notably, results from a Hong Kong offshore scenario show that the co-design framework attains a 10.7%-68.2% land-use reduction while preserving over 99.2\% of the maximum achievable AEP. By unlocking the land-sparing potential of wake steering, this study provides a novel paradigm to reconcile the wind capacity expansion with land conservation, thereby facilitating a more sustainable global energy transition.

title: Network Design and the Threshold for Explosive Growth
affiliations: Université de Poitiers

detail.title: Network Design and the Threshold for Explosive Growth
detail.abstract: Recent work shows that multi-sector innovation systems can exhibit explosive growth when the spectral radius of the cross-sector feedback matrix exceeds unity. Existing analyses typically treat this matrix as given. This paper instead studies a planner who allocates resources across spillover links and thereby chooses the network topology. The main result is that the marginal effect of strengthening any link on the spectral radius is proportional to the product of the corresponding left and right Perron eigenvector components. Optimal policy therefore directs investment toward links with the highest Perron-weighted return per unit cost. A key implication is that movement toward the explosive-growth threshold is driven by targeted strengthening of a small set of systemically central connections rather than broad-based increases in spillovers. An illustrative calibration based on U.S. input-output data, augmented with AI-related spillover parameters, shows how this mechanism generates highly concentrated optimal investment patterns. This provides a simple network-design perspective on technological acceleration.\end{abstract}

title: AI Capex Is Justified: A Bottom-Up Sectoral Estimate of Artificial Intelligence's Net Impact on US GDP
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: AI Capex Is Justified: A Bottom-Up Sectoral Estimate of Artificial Intelligence's Net Impact on US GDP
detail.abstract:
This paper presents a bottom-up sectoral model estimating the net annual impact of artificial intelligence on US GDP across 21 NAICS industries through 2036. Unlike top-down approaches that apply aggregate productivity multipliers to total output, the model restricts AI productivity gains to the labor-generated portion of each sector's gross value added — reducing the naive addressable base by approximately 72 percent. The core formula multiplies six inputs: base GDP, labor share, AI coverage, productivity gain percentage, adjusted adoption rate, and a skill-weighted capture rate. Three annual layers are added on top: demand expansion, a robotics unlock mechanism for physical sectors beginning in 2030, and an electricity drag that is subtracted each year.

AI coverage scores are sourced from Massenkoff and McCrory (2026), who introduce a measure of theoretical LLM task coverage across 22 Standard Occupational Classification groups. These scores are mapped to NAICS industries using employment-weighted averages derived from BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics data for 2023. Sector-specific productivity gain percentages are anchored to published evidence, including a randomised controlled trial of GitHub Copilot (Kalliamvakou et al., 2023), JPMorgan CEO disclosures, and Cognizant's New Work New World 2026 research. Regulatory and labor friction is scored per sector using actual compliance frameworks — Basel III, FDA AI guidance, HIPAA — and BLS union density data, and is applied as a haircut to base adoption rates via an S-curve ramp.

The model produces four scenarios differentiated by capture rate and friction assumptions. The base case yields approximately $1,057 billion in net annual GDP uplift by 2036, equivalent to 3.6 percent of 2024 GDP. The bear case produces $796 billion, the bull case $1,368 billion, and an agentic scenario — applying higher sector-specific productivity multiples consistent with full workflow transformation — produces $2,521 billion. In all four scenarios, cumulative net GDP exceeds cumulative AI infrastructure investment before 2036, with the base case achieving payback in 2033. Even excluding demand expansion and robotics layers entirely, the direct productivity contribution alone reaches approximately $940 billion per year by 2036.

The model identifies significant sectoral concentration: Professional and Technical Services, Information, and Finance and Insurance account for approximately 86 percent of the base case direct contribution. It also documents a distributional asymmetry consistent with Cognizant's (2026) internal findings: lower-skill workers exhibit higher individual productivity gains from AI tools than senior workers, but this does not automatically translate into proportional GDP capture given the skill-weighted capture rate framework applied here.

The paper documents 14 deliberate conservative assumptions — including frozen base GDP, no AI-on-AI compounding, a permanent friction floor, and conservative capture rates — all of which directionally understate the benefit. A sensitivity analysis shows that the high-skill capture rate and the pace of friction decay are the two parameters with the greatest influence on the aggregate result. The full model, including all 11 analytical tabs, is made publicly available to facilitate replication and independent sensitivity testing.

title: Smart Bets: Unequal Odds: A Case Study of Tax Bias in AI Gambling
affiliations: University of Alabama - School of Law and Rutgers University

detail.title: Smart Bets: Unequal Odds: A Case Study of Tax Bias in AI Gambling
detail.abstract: In the age of mobile wagering apps and algorithmic predictions, gambling has become ubiquitous, frictionless, and increasingly driven by artificial intelligence. This shift has been further accelerated by the emergence of AI-governed event-contract platforms that blur the line between gambling, prediction markets, and financial derivatives. Yet, while most participants lose money or break even, the federal tax system frequently taxes them as if they have realized economic gain. How so? High-income and sophisticated taxpayers are more likely to itemize deductions and offset gambling winnings with losses, while low-and middle-income taxpayers typically claim the standard deduction and receive no such offset. As a result, two taxpayers engaging in identical wagering or eventcontract activity can face radically different tax liabilities, including taxation on phantom income and the loss of other tax benefits. These disparities are exacerbated in AI-driven markets, where rapid, high-frequency transactions generate taxable "wins" divorced from economic reality. This Article exposes how the rise of AI-powered gambling and event-contract platforms has amplified a structural inequity embedded in the Internal Revenue Code. It argues that a statutory framework designed for an earlier era now disproportionately burdens taxpayers least equipped to anticipate or absorb these consequences. To address this inequity, the Article proposes three reform options reflecting distinct policy approaches: eliminating the deductibility of gambling losses altogether; permitting all recreational gamblers to deduct losses up to winnings; or imposing an excise tax on gambling winnings to fund the social costs of gambling. Any of these approaches would restore horizontal equity and eliminate the Code's largely accidental preference for high-income, sophisticated gamblers.

title: Stronger Evidence for Self-Serving Cognitive Flexibility: A Reproduction
affiliations: University of California, Davis, National Taiwan University - Department of Economics, and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Stronger Evidence for Self-Serving Cognitive Flexibility: A Reproduction
detail.abstract: We computationally reproduce Saccardo and Serra-Garcia (2023) where subjects exploit cognitive flexibility by viewing their incentives first and partially ignoring product quality information, and hence, recommend the incentivized product. We find one major coding error for the variable Selfishness. Additionally, two of the "moral cost" questions more likely capture spitefulness. After correcting the erroneous coding or dropping the two questions, we find stronger support for the authors' main conclusion regarding Selfishness driving incentive information avoidance with double effect size. Finally, we find weak evidence that subjects update their posterior beliefs differently depending on the product they are incentivized to recommend.

detail.abstract: We show that firms with labor market power can partially offset financial distress by financing through reduced worker compensation. Using U.S. Census quarterly employer-employee data, we find that workers in highly leveraged firms experience slower earnings growth following unexpected disinflation shocks that increase the real burden of firms' nominal debt. This response is stronger for firms with greater labor market power. We find no evidence of subsequent earnings compensation or increased worker separations, suggesting that workers remain despite relatively lower pay. We then develop a heterogeneous-firm model with labor market power and default risk. Quantitatively, labor market power mitigates about one-third of the negative effects of financial distress. This mitigation arises because, with heterogeneous firms, firm-specific wage adjustments through labor market power reduce misallocation and stabilize the economy more effectively than a uniform equilibrium wage decline in a competitive labor market.

title: Do Non-Competes Restrict Moonlighting for Physicians? Evidence From Policy Changes
affiliations: Humphrey School of Public Affairs and University of Nevada, Reno

detail.abstract: We study the effects of non-enforcement of non-compete agreements on the regional labor supply of physicians, exploiting statutory changes in Minnesota. We find two temporally distinct increases. The share of physicians moonlighting increased by 2.5 percentage points immediately after the non-enforcement, followed by later increases in the number of within-organization practice arrangements: 5.8 percent among early-career physicians and 7.9 percent among specialists. Overall, the number of healthcare services provided increased by 6.3 percent. Our findings suggest that relaxing regulatory barriers for the highly skilled regulated labor market would raise regional labor supply by increasing output at the intensive margin.

title: NGSE: From Symbolic Control Search to Mechanism Discovery in Swarm Robotics
affiliations: National University of Defense Technology, National University of Defense Technology, National University of Defense Technology, National University of Defense Technology and National University of Defense Technology

detail.title: NGSE: From Symbolic Control Search to Mechanism Discovery in Swarm Robotics
detail.abstract: Extracting explicit governing rules from evolved strategies remains a formidable challenge in swarm robotics. To address this, we propose a neural-guided symbolic evolution framework. Rather than treating controller design as a pure optimization task, we reformulate it as a process of interpretable mechanism discovery. By modeling symbolic evolution as a sequential decision process, the system utilizes graph neural networks and Monte Carlo tree search to efficiently identify high-performance velocity controllers within a vast combinatorial space of physical hypotheses. A key contribution is the integration of an large language models-driven interpreter that performs semantic decompilation on the evolved formulas. This allows the framework to autonomously distill raw mathematical expressions into human-readable physical mechanisms, such as virtual damping and potential field shaping. Validated across flocking, formation, and entrapping tasks, NGSE demonstrates the ability to not only match the performance of deep reinforcement learning but also to recover the underlying coordination logic, marking a shift from automated control synthesis to AI-assisted knowledge extraction in complex systems.

title: Call option pressure and option return predictability: A U-shaped nonlinearity
affiliations: Zhejiang University

detail.title: Call option pressure and option return predictability: A U-shaped nonlinearity
detail.abstract: This paper constructs a call pressure index (CP) from China's SSE 50 ETF option market and finds a robust U-shaped nonlinear predictability for directional option returns as measured by log returns. The effect reflects that extreme call pressures—whether unusually low (reversal) or high (momentum)—contain information, while moderate levels are dominated by noise trading. Robustness checks using delta-hedged returns confirm that predictability stems primarily from directional exposure rather than volatility dynamics. The predictability is stronger in high-volatility and down-market states and survives controlling for implied skewness, variance risk premium, and other common predictors. A simple timing strategy based on rolling-window forecasts achieves a Sharpe ratio of 0.97, which further increases to 2.43 after applying a prediction threshold. A parsimonious volume-based indicator captures unique predictive information beyond complex proxies, offering a feasible path for emerging markets lacking proprietary order flow data.

title: Assessing the Applicability of Evidence-based Design and Planning: A Multi-scale Approach for Data-challenging Environments
affiliations: University of Cyprus, University of Cyprus, University of Cyprus, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University College London

detail.title: Assessing the Applicability of Evidence-based Design and Planning: A Multi-scale Approach for Data-challenging Environments
detail.abstract: Evidence-Based Design and Planning (EBDP) provides a systematic framework for informing urban design and planning decisions by grounding proposals in data, analysis, and stakeholder input. However, its practical application remains limited and challenging, particularly in contexts where spatial data are fragmented, institutional capacities are weak, and mechanisms for integrating evidence into decision-making are underdeveloped. This paper advances the applicability of EBDP by developing an adaptable methodology suitable for diverse planning contexts, including those with incomplete or inconsistent datasets and institutional fragmentation. The proposed approach integrates targeted data collection, stakeholder engagement, and both hybrid and automated spatial modelling techniques. To evaluate the feasibility of applying EBDP in specific contexts, the study introduces an EBDP Applicability Matrix, a readiness tool that assesses key enabling conditions such as data availability, technical competence, policy alignment, and stakeholder support. The methodology and matrix were tested across three Cypriot case studies at local, regional, and national scales. Findings demonstrate that the approach improves data acquisition, structures stakeholder collaboration, and enables ongoing and verifiable goal achievement through the use of reliable spatial analysis. The paper contributes an auditable EBDP workflow, a readiness matrix for feasibility screening, and guidance on institutional and data prerequisites supporting EBDP adoption.

title: How do climate-resilient city pilots deliver ecological co-benefits? Causal evidence on urban habitat quality with nonlinear thresholds
affiliations: Ningbo University, Ningbo University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Ningbo University

detail.title: How do climate-resilient city pilots deliver ecological co-benefits? Causal evidence on urban habitat quality with nonlinear thresholds
detail.abstract: Amid accelerating climate change and rapid urbanization, it is essential to understand whether climate adaptation policies generate ecological co-benefits and under what conditions they are most effective. Using China’s Climate-Resilient City Pilot (CRP) as a large-scale policy experiment, this study evaluates its impacts on urban habitat quality and examines how effectiveness varies across spatial governance and investment contexts. We combine a quasi-experimental Difference-in-Differences design with Double Machine Learning (DID-DML) to obtain credible causal estimates under high-dimensional confounding, and apply XGBoost with SHAP interaction analysis to identify nonlinear pathways and threshold effects. Using panel data for 300 Chinese cities from 2010 to 2022, we find that the CRP significantly improves habitat quality (average effect=0.0275), with stronger impacts two years after adoption (0.0677) and pronounced regional heterogeneity. Mechanism analysis indicates that the CRP increases public fiscal expenditure, yielding a sizable indirect effect (0.060), while the green-space expansion channel is statistically insignificant. Nonlinear results further show that marginal policy effects strengthen when fiscal revenue exceeds 500 million CNY and vary non-monotonically with green space coverage, declining to around 35% before rebounding to approximately 40%. These findings move beyond average treatment effects to provide actionable thresholds for targeting adaptation investments, prioritizing functional green-space upgrading over simple expansion, and aligning fiscal incentives with ecological performance.

title: Deep Kinetic JKO schemes for Vlasov-Fokker-Planck Equations
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Minnesota - Minneapolis and University of South Carolina

detail.title: Deep Kinetic JKO schemes for Vlasov-Fokker-Planck Equations
detail.abstract: We introduce a deep neural network-based numerical method for solving kinetic Fokker Planck equations, including both linear and nonlinear cases. Building upon the conservative dissipative structure of Vlasov-type equations, we formulate a class of generalized minimizing movement schemes as iterative constrained minimization problems: the conservative part determines the constraint set, while the dissipative part defines the objective functional. This leads to an analog of the classical Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto (JKO) scheme for Wasserstein gradient flows, and we refer to it as the kinetic JKO scheme. To compute each step of the kinetic JKO iteration, we introduce a particle-based approximation in which the velocity field is parameterized by deep neural networks. The resulting algorithm can be interpreted as a kinetic-oriented neural differential equation that enables the representation of high-dimensional kinetic dynamics while preserving the essential variational and structural properties of the underlying PDE. We validate the method with extensive numerical experiments and demonstrate that the proposed kinetic JKO-neural ODE framework is effective for high-dimensional numerical simulations.

title: Symbiosis with Penicillium sp. D7 Rewires Molecular Modules to Boost Plant Growth and As(III) Stress Tolerance
affiliations: Instituto Nacional de Investigación y Tecnología Agraria y Alimentaria (INA), Instituto Nacional de Investigación y Tecnología Agraria y Alimentaria (INA), University Abdelmalek Essaâdi, Faculty of Sciences and Techniques of Tangier, Instituto Nacional de Investigación y Tecnología Agraria y Alimentaria (INA), Instituto Nacional de Investigación y Tecnología Agraria y Alimentaria (INA), Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM) - Centro de Biotecnología y Genómica de Plantas and Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM) - Centro de Biotecnología y Genómica de Plantas

detail.title: Symbiosis with Penicillium sp. D7 Rewires Molecular Modules to Boost Plant Growth and As(III) Stress Tolerance
detail.abstract: Arsenic (As) contamination severely compromises plant growth and agricultural productivity, particularly in environments affected by mining or industrial activities. Microbial symbionts adapted to metalliferous soils represent a promising yet underexploited resource for enhancing plant tolerance to As toxicity. In this study, we isolated root-associated fungal endophytes from three plant species thriving on As-rich tailings of the Mónica mine (Bustaviejo, Spain) and identified Penicillium sp. strain D7 as a highly As-tolerant symbiont with pronounced plant growth–promoting effects. When co-cultivated with Arabidopsis thaliana, D7 significantly enhanced shoot biomass under As(III) stress and mitigated characteristic toxicity symptoms. Transcriptome profiling revealed that D7 reprograms plant hormone signalling of the host in a tissue-specific manner: the fungus suppresses abscisic acid (ABA) biosynthesis and ABA-responsive stress pathways in roots, while simultaneously inducing auxin biosynthesis and signalling in shoots, consistent with improved growth performance. Furthermore, D7 elicited the coordinated induction of key components of the plant’s intrinsic As detoxification machinery, including ARQ1, PCS1, and the vacuolar transporters ABCC1 and ABCC2. Functional analyses using the abcc1 abcc2 double mutant demonstrated that vacuolar sequestration of As(III) in roots is essential for D7-mediated stress tolerance, indicating that fungal colonisation enhances the host’s capacity for intracellular detoxification rather than reducing As uptake. Together, these results demonstrate that Penicillium sp. D7 reinforces plant resilience to As(III) by simultaneously attenuating stress perception, promoting growth-related hormonal programs, and stimulating vacuolar sequestration of As. This study highlights D7 as a promising microbial tool for supporting vegetation establishment and phytostabilisation efforts in As-contaminated environments.

title: From Switching to Sharing: A Micro-Process Theory of Shared Leadership–Shared Followership
affiliations: Universidad Diego Portales, Universidad de Tarapaca and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: From Switching to Sharing: A Micro-Process Theory of Shared Leadership–Shared Followership
detail.abstract: Despite its well-documented benefits, the micro-behavioral mechanisms driving shared leadership emergence remain a theoretical "black box." To resolve this explanatory gap, we advance a micro-process theory positing that shared leadership inherently requires shared followership. We introduce Leader–Follower Switching Behavior (LFS-B)—the capacity to fluidly alternate between claiming and granting influence—as the behavioral micro-foundation of team leadership structure. Testing this account across 61 mature healthcare teams (233 individuals) using a three-level, multi-occasion design, we demonstrate how episodic micro-behaviors systematically compile into macro-level networks. Crucially, we disentangle network amount from structural pattern: LFS-B Magnitude (total role volume) drives overarching network density, while LFS-B Balance (role symmetry) uniquely drives reciprocal mutuality (Importance-Weighted Density) and dismantles hierarchical centralization. Furthermore, our variance decomposition reveals a temporal paradox of task demands: acute episodic difficulty triggers adaptive role-switching, whereas chronic team difficulty induces structural threat-rigidity, severely suppressing LFS-B. Finally, we demonstrate that interpersonal trust climate, rather than stable Big Five personality traits, serves as the primary enabler of this behavioral duality. This research shifts the field's focus from static leader emergence to the dynamic, co-created mechanics of how switching becomes structure.

title: Visual vs. textual communication: Impact on firms’ inflation expectations and central bank credibility
affiliations: Central Bank of Uruguay, Central Bank of Uruguay and Central Bank of Uruguay

detail.title: Visual vs. textual communication: Impact on firms’ inflation expectations and central bank credibility
detail.abstract: We causally identify how firms’ inflation expectations and their trust in the central bank respond to information with the same relevant content presented through different formats in a desinflationary environment. Simple text and visual communication effectively influence inflation expectations, while complex text messaging fails to yield similar effects. Firms exposed to visual representations of information adjust their expectations significantly more than those receiving equivalent information in text form. Notably, the effect of visual content is particularly strong but short-lived. Complex text messages may undermine the credibility of the central bank. These results suggest a scope for tailoring communication to better align firms’ inflation expectations with inflation targets while preserving the credibility of the monetary authority.

title: Multi-scale dynamic cross-modal fusion for carbon price forecasting with dual-channel textual semantics and bidirectional cross-attention
affiliations: Guangxi University and Guangxi University

detail.title: Multi-scale dynamic cross-modal fusion for carbon price forecasting with dual-channel textual semantics and bidirectional cross-attention
detail.abstract: Carbon prices in emissions trading systems (ETS) are increasingly influenced not only by energy and macroeconomic conditions, but also by policy communication, regulatory expectations, and public sentiment conveyed through textual information. However, most existing studies treat text as a homogeneous contemporaneous signal, which limits understanding of how heterogeneous semantic components shape carbon price dynamics across temporal horizons. This study develops a multi-scale dynamic feature fusion framework based on deep learning to examine the scale-dependent impacts of textual information on carbon prices. A dual-channel text representation scheme is constructed to disentangle short-term sentiment-driven shocks from medium- to long-term policy and regulatory semantics. The carbon price series is decomposed and reconstructed into scale-specific components, aligning semantic horizons with corresponding price fluctuations for a scale-aware assessment of textual effects. To capture time-varying and potentially asymmetric interactions between textual and numerical information, a bidirectional cross-attention mechanism is embedded within each scale-specific sub-model, allowing cross-modal dependencies to adapt to evolving market conditions. Forecasting is conducted with an attention-enhanced bidirectional long short-term memory network (Bi-LSTM), and Bayesian optimization is employed for robust hyperparameter tuning. Empirical results from the Hubei and Guangzhou markets suggest that the proposed framework delivers competitive and stable forecasting performance compared with benchmark methods, while offering empirical evidence of scale-dependent and time-varying textual influences, supporting the usefulness of scale-aware and semantically differentiated text integration for carbon price prediction.

title: Structural Amplification in Organisational Crises: How Authority, Dependence, and Governance Reconfigure the Transmission of Leadership Influence
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Structural Amplification in Organisational Crises: How Authority, Dependence, and Governance Reconfigure the Transmission of Leadership Influence
detail.abstract: Organisational crises are widely associated with heightened leadership impact, yet existing leadership theory offers limited explanation for why leadership influence appears amplified under such conditions. This article develops a theory of structural amplification, which reconceptualises leadership influence as a function of how strongly leadership signals are transmitted through organisational systems.The framework argues that crisis conditions increase the coupling between leadership behaviour and organisational outcomes by activating three reinforcing structural mechanisms: authority expansion, interpretive dependence, and governance relaxation. These mechanisms concentrate decision authority, heighten reliance on leadership sensegiving, and reduce institutional constraints, thereby strengthening the transmission of leadership signals across the organisation.These structural shifts are further reinforced by behavioural dynamics—cognitive compression, relational asymmetry, and voice suppression—which increase responsiveness to leadership cues under conditions of uncertainty and urgency. Together, these structural and behavioural processes amplify the variance of leadership outcomes, increasing the likelihood of both exceptional success and catastrophic failure.By shifting attention from leader behaviour to the organisational conditions that govern influence transmission, this article advances leadership theory in three ways. First, it explains why the magnitude of leadership influence varies across contexts. Second, it integrates insights from leadership, crisis management, governance, and organisational behaviour into a unified framework. Third, it provides a system-level account of when strong leadership effects reflect substantive organisational dynamics rather than attributional bias.The article concludes by outlining boundary conditions and propositions to support future empirical research on leadership in crisis and extreme contexts.

title: Privatization Without Accountability? The Collapse of China's CAS Journal Ranking and Its Implications for Research Evaluation Reform
affiliations: Hangzhou Dianzi University

detail.title: Privatization Without Accountability? The Collapse of China's CAS Journal Ranking and Its Implications for Research Evaluation Reform
detail.abstract: In March 2026, China's most influential journal-classification tool — the Journal Partition Table maintained by the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) — was abruptly discontinued and replaced by a privately operated entity with opaque governance. Simultaneously, CAS imposed restrictions on using public funds to pay article-processing charges at over 30 high-cost international open-access journals. These twin disruptions expose a fundamental tension in China's research evaluation reform: between the stated ambition to move "beyond metrics" and the persistent institutional reliance on journal-tier classifications for hiring, promotion, and degree conferral. This paper argues that the privatization of China's journal-ranking infrastructure, absent meaningful transparency reforms, risks entrenching rather than dismantling metrics-driven evaluation — by removing public accountability while preserving the incentive structures that make journal tiers consequential. We situate the Chinese case within the global landscape of research assessment reform, drawing comparisons with the abolition of journal rankings in Australia's ERA system, the emergence of the Coalition for Advancing Research Assessment (CoARA) in Europe, and the commercial model of Clarivate's Journal Citation Reports. We conclude that journal-ranking transitions offer a critical but underutilized window for systemic evaluation reform, and that China's experience holds lessons for any research system grappling with the politics of dismantling entrenched bibliometric infrastructure.

title: A REPLICABLE CASH-FLOW STRESS INDEX FOR CENTRAL BANK LIQUIDITY SUSTAINABILITY: EVIDENCE FROM THAILAND (2005–2024)
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Jadara University

detail.title: A REPLICABLE CASH-FLOW STRESS INDEX FOR CENTRAL BANK LIQUIDITY SUSTAINABILITY: EVIDENCE FROM THAILAND (2005–2024)
detail.abstract: Central bank liquidity sustainability is increasingly critical in emerging markets facing volatile capital flows and repeated external shocks. However, conventional macro-financial indicators, such as foreign reserves and policy rates, often fail to capture internal fragility arising from cash-flow imbalances and rising sterilization costs. This study addresses this gap by proposing a replicable cash-flow-based index framework to assess central bank financial sustainability using Bank of Thailand data over the period 2005–2024. The methodology is constructed with two complementary indicators: the Central Bank Cash-Flow Stress Index (CB-CFSI), measuring liquidity stress relative to cash buffers, and the Sterilization Cost Stress Index (SCSI), capturing interest-expense pressure. Both indices are normalized and combined into a composite measure to identify vulnerability conditions. The novelty lies in shifting analysis from external macro indicators to internal cash-flow structures and introducing a dual-index, period-based monitoring approach. The results show that financial stress does not increase gradually, but appears in certain phase, with the highest vulnerability occurring during 2005–2010, especially around the global financial crisis. Although conditions become more stable after 2011, occasional increases indicate that the system remains sensitive to external shocks and changes in interest rates; therefore, this study tries to contribute by providing a practical early-warning tool that can improve monitoring, support policy decisions, and help investors better assess risk in emerging markets.

title: Firm-Level Trade Responses to Intellectual Property Reforms: Evidence from India
affiliations: Indian Institute of Foreign Trade, Indira Gandhi Institute of Development Research and Indian Institute of Foreign Trade

detail.title: Firm-Level Trade Responses to Intellectual Property Reforms: Evidence from India
detail.abstract: This study examines how strengthening of domestic intellectual property rights (IPRs) shapes firm-level trade and global value chain (GVC) integration in an emerging economy. Leveraging India’s Patents (Amendment) Act, 2002 as a quasi-natural experiment, we employ a difference-in-differences framework to compare outcomes across high-tech and low-tech manufacturing firms. Using comprehensive firm-level panel data, we find that heightened  patent protection is associated with an 18% increase in exports and a 12% increase in total imports for high-tech firms relative to low-tech counterparts, under a rich set of fixed effects. Decomposing import responses, we show a 20% rise in imports of raw materials-suggesting enhanced technology adoption and access to advanced inputs-but a significant decline in imports of spare parts and stores, indicating potential shifts in domestic sourcing or maintenance practices. While average treatment effects on capital and finished goods imports remain insignificant, event-study estimates reveal positive and significant effects albeit with a delay. These findings provide policy-relevant evidence that stronger IPR regimes in emerging economies can improve trade performance by stimulating innovation, facilitating technology transfer, and reshaping input sourcing strategies along GVCs.

title: Third-party facilitation in the emergence of polycentric governance for urban logistics: The case of France
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Third-party facilitation in the emergence of polycentric governance for urban logistics: The case of France
detail.abstract: While local authorities are required to develop and implement coherent public policies to support sustainable urban logistics, the establishment of appropriate governance structures is attracting increasing attention. However, several obstacles continue to hinder the emergence and structuring of local collective action, revealing the need for support provided by a third party. The inherent complexity of urban logistics requires the definition of national guidelines and coordination of policies implemented at different levels. To address this, this study explored the evolving role of a national third party that addresses the barriers identified during the initiation and formalization of local governance and contributes to the emergence of multi-level governance in France. This study drew on 63 semi-structured interviews conducted with public and private stakeholders across six case studies: four local governance bodies and two national bodies. We first observed that local governance is perceived as a burden for local authorities, which third parties offset by supporting the emergence, structuring, and stabilization of organizational and relational processes over time. Identified locally as a collaborative toolbox, the third party also contributes to the emergence of the polycentric governance of urban logistics by occupying a central position within the French ecosystem. Given the limited duration of some third-party interventions, such as national programs, our conclusions emphasize the need to develop institutions to ensure the continuity of local support and the sustainability of dialogue spaces conducive to the development of polycentric governance.

title: The Sum of All (Workplace) Fears: How Managers Mediate the Fear of AI Job Displacement

detail.title: The Sum of All (Workplace) Fears: How Managers Mediate the Fear of AI Job Displacement
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence is transforming work, but workers' responses to these technologies depend not only on exposure to AI, but also on how organizations, especially managers, oversee the transition. Using longitudinal data from the Gallup Workforce Panel from 2023 to 2026, I examine whether managers and workplace practices shape employees' fears that AI will eliminate their jobs. Although only 3-4 percent of workers say their job is very likely to disappear within five years, and 14-19 percent say it is somewhat or very likely, concern is substantially higher among frequent AI users. Stronger workplace practices are associated with meaningfully lower displacement fear: a one-standard-deviation increase in workplace quality is associated with about 13 to 24 percent lower odds of reporting greater displacement risk, and workers reporting the highest level of organizational wellbeing support are 6-6.8 percentage points less likely to say their job is somewhat or very likely to be displaced. While frequent AI use raises perceived displacement risk by 6.0 percentage points, but this increase is offset by up to 9.0 percentage points among workers in high-wellbeing workplaces. In short, managers play a central role in shaping how workers interpret AI adoption.

title: Recognizing meteorological drivers of wind and solar electricity droughts: Observational evidence from a province in China
affiliations: Dalian University of Technology, Dalian University of Technology and Dalian University of Technology

detail.title: Recognizing meteorological drivers of wind and solar electricity droughts: Observational evidence from a province in China

keywords.keywords: Variable renewable energy； extreme fluctuations；meteorological factors；driving mechanisms

detail.abstract: Extreme w eather-induced wind and solar electricity droughts (WSEDs) can seriously disrupt the electricity balance in power systems with high shares of variable renewable energy (VRE). However, the limited availability of long-term time-series VRE output data has prevented previous studies from systematically investigating the characteristics of WSEDs and quantitatively identifying their meteorological drivers. This is particularly the case in countries such as China and India, where VRE deployment has only recently accelerated. Therefore, this study collected VRE output records from 2016 to 2024 for Yunnan  provincial  power grid in China, one of the earliest provinces to deploy VRE on a large scale.  Based on a novel mathematical formulation of WSEDs, this study established China's first provincial-level WSED event dataset. Analysis reveals that wind and solar electricity droughts occurred approximately nine and six times per year respectively, with over 90% of events lasting 2-4 days, while compound droughts remained considerably rarer at approximately two occurrences annually. Analysis of driving mechanisms demonstrates that wind electricity droughts were primarily triggered by wind speed deficits exceeding 55.5% below monthly averages, or smaller deficits occurring alongside temperature declines. Solar power droughts required radiation drops over 65.2% below normal, or milder anomalies accompanied by concurrent temperature reductions of 15.9%, where precipitation further lowered triggering thresholds.  The results provide new support for Yunnan Power Grid in China to defend against WSEDs. Specifically, the occurrence of potential WSEDs can be predicted by forecasting fluctuations in meteorological factors, allowing proactive responses through measures such as energy storage deployment. Meanwhile, meteorological factors that may trigger more severe WSEDs should be closely monitored.

title: Research on Predicting Blasting Vibration Peak Particle Velocity Based on Improved Bayesian Optimization
affiliations: Shenyang Jianzhu University, Shenyang Jianzhu University and Shenyang Jianzhu University

detail.title: Research on Predicting Blasting Vibration Peak Particle Velocity Based on Improved Bayesian Optimization
detail.abstract: Blasting serves as a critical technique for mineral resource extraction. Blasting-induced vibrational energy propagates through rock media and can readily cause significant adverse impacts on nearby structures, the ecological environment, and human comfort. To mitigate the hazards associated with blasting vibrations, we propose a prediction method for Peak Particle Velocity (PPV) based on an improved Bayesian optimization algorithm. Utilizing a database containing 88 PPV records, the dataset was partitioned into training and testing subsets at an 8:2 ratio. The improved Bayesian optimization method was employed to tune the hyperparameters of four predictive models: Ensemble Tree (ET), Kernel Ridge Regression (KRR), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Efficient Linear (EL). Model performance for each hyperparameter set was evaluated using a 10-fold cross-validation approach, enabling a comparative assessment of the superiority of these prediction models. The results indicate that the SVM and EL models optimized by this method achieve prediction accuracy significantly superior to that of the ET and KRR models, demonstrating robust generalization capability. We provide a valuable reference for controlling rock mass stability in bench blasting operations in open-pit mines.

title: Multi-step reliable interval prediction of wind farm power with wake-aware spatio-temporal coupling
affiliations: Xinjiang University, Xinjiang University, Xinjiang University, Xinjiang University, Xinjiang University and Xinjiang University

detail.title: Multi-step reliable interval prediction of wind farm power with wake-aware spatio-temporal coupling
detail.abstract: As power systems integrate higher shares of renewable energy, wind power forecasting is increasingly required to support reserve allocation, operational balancing and risk-aware dispatch. Yet ultra-short-term wind farm forecasting remains difficult because wake propagation continuously reshapes inter-turbine dependence, static spatial models cannot adequately represent directed and time-varying interactions, and multi-step interval forecasts often become miscalibrated or unstable under disturbed operating conditions. Here we present RWGF, a unified framework for reliable multi-step wind farm power forecasting that combines dynamic wake-aware spatial modelling with horizon-wise uncertainty control. RWGF constructs a dynamic directed wake graph from turbine layout, real-time wind conditions and wake velocity-deficit physics, and couples it with multi-scale spatio-temporal learning to capture evolving wake interactions and non-stationary temporal patterns. On this basis, future intervals are generated through non-crossing quantile learning with horizon-wise width and boundary-smoothness regularisation and are further refined by step-wise conformal recalibration. Experiments on SCADA data from two real-world wind farms show that RWGF improves both deterministic accuracy and the coverage-sharpness trade-off of interval prediction, while remaining more robust under intense turbulence and rapid ramping. These results show that physically informed dynamic spatial modelling and horizon-aware calibration can improve the operational value of wind power forecasting for renewable-rich power systems.

title: Towards Net-Zero Building: An Optimisation Methodology for Passive and Active Retrofits with Renewable Integration - A UK Office Building Case Study
affiliations: Durham University and Durham University

detail.title: Towards Net-Zero Building: An Optimisation Methodology for Passive and Active Retrofits with Renewable Integration - A UK Office Building Case Study
detail.abstract: Existing commercial buildings account for a large share of energy use and carbon emissions, highlighting the need for net-zero retrofit strategies. This study develops an integrated framework for building retrofits, combining calibrated building energy simulation with multi-source renewable energy system design and optimisation to reduce energy demand, maximise on-site renewable generation, and enable cost-effective decarbonisation. A calibrated energy model was created in DesignBuilder to evaluate retrofit measures, while renewable energy systems and storage were optimised using HOMER Pro. A two-stage MATLAB-based Pareto front and TOPSIS multi-criteria optimisation evaluated and ranked retrofit configurations. The framework was applied to a case-study UK office building (hot-summer, cold-winter climate), identifying the optimal configuration, which combines lighting upgrades, office equipment improvements, a water-to-water ground-source heat pump, carport-mounted solar PV, and rooftop horizontal-axis wind turbines. The retrofit reduced annual energy demand by 38.4\% and achieved an average renewable fraction of 66.3\%, with on-site generation exceeding demand during peak months. Annual CO$_2$ emissions decrease by 39.0\% after retrofitting and by 86.1\% after the integration of renewables compared to the baseline model of the case-study building. Economic analysis shows strong financial viability, with a levelised cost of £0.172/kWh and a payback period of 6.48 years. Sensitivity analyses confirm the solution remains optimal under varying energy prices and stakeholder priorities, demonstrating robustness for commercial deployment. The results highlight the framework’s ability to guide transferable, multi-criteria retrofit planning and support deep operational decarbonisation across diverse building types.

title: INARA: Intelligent Neural Atmospheric Retrieval Algorithm
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: INARA: Intelligent Neural Atmospheric Retrieval Algorithm
detail.abstract: The characterization of exoplanet atmospheres is fundamental to understanding planetary diversity and identifying potentially habitable worlds. However, traditional atmospheric retrieval methods based on Bayesian inference are computationally intensive, often requiring hours to days per spectrum. This creates a critical bottleneck as the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and future missions like ARIEL produce vast quantities of high-quality spectral data. We present INARA (Intelligent Neural Atmospheric Retrieval Algorithm), an open-source deep learning framework that accelerates atmospheric retrieval by three orders of magnitude while maintaining statistical consistency with established radiative transfer codes.INARA comprises a forward model for generating synthetic transmission spectra, a multi-branch neural network with variational autoencoder (VAE) for parameter estimation with uncertainty quantification, and a comprehensive validation suite. A dataset of 50,000 synthetic exoplanet atmospheres spanning nine molecular species was generated using the petitRADTRANS framework. The neural network, optimized via Keras-Tuner, achieves a coefficient of determination R² = 0.95 on held-out test data. Temperature scaling reduces the Expected Calibration Error (ECE) from 0.031 to 0.018, yielding well-calibrated uncertainty estimates.Validation on 20 public JWST targets (both real and realistically simulated) demonstrates a mean inference time of 0.28 s per spectrum, with 84.2% of retrieved parameters falling within 1σ of literature values. A benchmark suite of 200 synthetic spectra compared against petitRADTRANS and TauREx retrievals shows a median absolute deviation of 0.41 dex and a posterior overlap coefficient of 0.79, confirming statistical consistency. Robustness tests against six instrumental systematics reveal minimal degradation (median factor 1.02). INARA is not a biosignature detection tool; it is an acceleration layer designed to enable rapid, population-level atmospheric studies. All code, trained models, and datasets are publicly available at https://github.com/gargi-t/iris.

title: Large Language Models for Minimum Data Set Documentation Support in Skilled Nursing Facilities: Opportunities, Risks, and a Proposed Implementation Framework

detail.title: Large Language Models for Minimum Data Set Documentation Support in Skilled Nursing Facilities: Opportunities, Risks, and a Proposed Implementation Framework

declarations.declarationOfInterest: no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not required — literature review and framework proposal, no human subjects
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: Background: The Minimum Data Set (MDS) is the federally mandated clinical assessment instrument used in all Medicare-and Medicaid-certified skilled nursing facilities (SNFs) in the United States. Comprising more than 600 coded data elements and governed by strict submission timelines, MDS documentation imposes a considerable administrative burden on nursing staff and is directly linked to reimbursement accuracy under the Patient-Driven Payment Model (PDPM). Large language models (LLMs) have shown the capacity to reduce documentation time in acute and ambulatory care settings, yet no peer-reviewed work has examined their application to the structured, regulatory, and SNF-specific demands of MDS documentation. Objectives: We identify and characterize the literature gap at the intersection of LLMs and MDS documentation, synthesize existing evidence on LLM deployment in clinical documentation more broadly, and propose an implementation framework tailored to the regulatory, workforce, and interoperability constraints of SNF environments. Methods: We conducted a structured literature search across PubMed, IEEE Xplore, Scopus, and CINAHL using terms combining large language model, LLM, GPT, minimum data set, MDS, skilled nursing, nursing home, and long-term care documentation. We supplemented this search with a review of current CMS regulatory updates, HIPAA guidance, and the HL7 FHIR R4 interoperability standard relevant to SNF data infrastructure. Results: Our search identified zero peer-reviewed publications on LLM application to MDS documentation, despite 41 studies confirming LLM utility in general clinical documentation. We present a three-mode implementation framework-Draft Assist, Consistency Checker, and Query Interface-grounded in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture using the CMS Resident Assessment Instrument (RAI) Manual as the knowledge base. We further propose a risk taxonomy specific to SNF-LLM deployment covering hallucination, automation bias, regulatory liability, and data governance. Conclusion: LLMs represent a high-potential, under-explored tool for reducing MDS documentation burden in SNFs. The proposed framework provides a translational roadmap for researchers, EHR vendors, and SNF administrators seeking to responsibly evaluate and deploy LLM-assisted documentation support. Future work should prioritize prospective pilot studies using de-identified or synthetic MDS datasets.

title: A Future-Oriented Taxonomy for Higher Education Institutional Research Offices and Positions

detail.abstract: This paper proposes a future-oriented taxonomy for Institutional Research offices and positions in higher education, arguing that traditional conceptions of Institutional Research are no longer sufficient to address the increasing complexity of institutional data environments, advanced analytics, artificial intelligence, and real-time decision support. Reframing Institutional Research as an evolving institutional intelligence function, the paper examines how roles and organizational structures may develop across projected horizons of 2030, 2040, and 2050, moving from centralized reporting and compliance functions toward strategically embedded, distributed, and ethically governed intelligence systems. The taxonomy outlines the transformation of both office models and professional roles, including shifts from reporting and analysis to data orchestration, predictive modeling, algorithmic governance, decision systems consultation, and institutional foresight. Ultimately, the paper contends that the future of Institutional Research will depend on its ability to integrate technological sophistication with ethical stewardship, human judgment, and mission-driven institutional adaptation, offering a conceptual framework to guide the field’s continued evolution in higher education.

detail.abstract: This study looks at how social media use affects the mental health and behavior of people from Generation Z. As digital platforms become more part of everyday life, social media has a big influence on how people feel, how they see themselves, and how they interact with others. The research is based on data gathered from a survey given to over 100 people. It looks into how much time people spend on social media, how they feel emotionally, how they compare themselves to others, and their overall mental health. The results show that while social media helps people stay connected and informed, using it too much can cause stress, lower self-confidence, and changes in behavior. The study also points out the importance of using social media wisely and being aware of its effects on young people.

detail.title: Reducing Subjectivity in Liquid Penetrant Inspectionof Welds through Computer Vision
detail.abstract: The inspection of welded joints is a critical process in industrial environments where structural integrity and safety must be ensured. Traditional liquid penetrant testing is effective but can be limited by subjective visual assessment, variability across inspectors, and human error. This work presents an automated inspection pipeline that integrates liquid penetrant testing with artificial intelligence and computer vision. The proposed approach employs convolutional neural networks to analyze weld images and classify five surface conditions/discontinuity types, aligned with standards such as American Society for Testing and Materials E165/E165M and International Organization for Standardization 3452. Model selection is performed on a development set via stratified 10-fold cross-validation with fixed, reproducible folds, and the final evaluation is reported on a held-out test set. Performance is quantified using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, and interpretability is supported via Grad-CAM++ visual explanations. Under this protocol, the proposed convolutional network achieves the best overall cross-validation performance among the evaluated deep and shallow baselines.

title: Evaluative Crowding in Financial Markets: Shared Objective Structures and Strategy Convergence
affiliations: Lex et Ratio Ltd

detail.title: Evaluative Crowding in Financial Markets: Shared Objective Structures and Strategy Convergence
detail.abstract: This article examines a recurring empirical pattern in financial markets: strategies constructed on heterogeneous data and models nevertheless converge in positioning and unwind in a highly synchronized manner under stress. Episodes such as the August 2007 quant crisis, the March 2020 cross-asset dislocation, and the 2022 UK liability-driven investment (LDI) episode exhibit this structure. Existing explanations based on liquidity, leverage, and funding constraints account for the amplification of shocks but do not fully explain why positions are aligned ex ante. The article advances a complementary mechanism—evaluative crowding—through which convergence arises from shared transformation rather than shared inputs. Agents optimize under evaluative structures ℓ∈L, comprising risk operators, admissibility constraints, and objective functions. When these structures are partially aligned across institutions—through common risk models, constraints, and implementation infrastructure—heterogeneous signals are mapped through a common operator Φℓ, inducing clustering in admissible strategies without requiring shared information or coordination. A tractable game-theoretic model characterises the structural implications of shared evaluative mappings. When evaluative operators exhibit low effective dimensionality—a standard feature of factor-based risk models—optimal portfolios concentrate in a restricted subspace. Within this framework, alignment arises as a property of shared transformations rather than shared positions, and a formal distinction emerges between first-order failures (performance deterioration within a fixed evaluative structure) and second-order failures (misalignment of the evaluative structure itself). When evaluative structures are fixed over relevant horizons, perturbations to the mapping from signals to strategies generate correlated adjustments across agents, producing synchronized responses under stress. The article derives empirically testable implications, including convergence conditional on evaluative structure, discrete shifts in evaluative frameworks around crisis events, break-type adjustment dynamics, and regime-dependent persistence in positioning. These implications distinguish evaluative crowding from factor-based and ownership-based mechanisms under appropriate controls. A stylized simulation, matched to an analytic benchmark, demonstrates that, in the stylised setting, dispersion compression and directional alignment are fully determined by the spectral properties of the evaluative operator under isotropic inputs. The results imply that systemic fragility depends not only on balance sheet constraints and market liquidity, but also on the structure of evaluation governing decision-making.

title: Cyanobacterial Concentrations Cause Significant Welfare Declines to Recreational Fisheries: Evidence From a Bloom-Prone Urban Lake

detail.abstract: Chlorophyll-a is widely monitored as an indicator of bloom conditions, yet managers often lack a defensible way to translate sporadic measurements into decision-relevant recreation outcomes. We develop and demonstrate a replicable, threshold-based indicator-to-outcome workflow for bloom-prone fisheries. During 27 site-days in 2022, we intercepted 384 visitors; 290 completed surveys (75.5% response rate), of which, 174 anglers formed the analytic sample. Anglers provided repeated photo-based ratings of water suitability for fishing; random-effects ordered probit models were used to estimate a user-defined aesthetic threshold and to convert chl-a into a perceived quality index. Next, we built a daily lake-wide chl-a time series for 2022 to bridge temporal data gaps in irregular in-situ observations. This was done by training a histogram gradient-boosting model that captured the temporal structure of chl-a concentrations, supporting use as an operational daily indicator under sparse sampling. Predicted chl-a exceeded the angler-defined threshold (58.3 µg/L) 83 days of the year, including a 35-day stretch during peak summer demand. We then embedded the quality index in a single-site negative binomial travel cost model to estimate welfare and translate indicator exceedances into outcome losses. The estimated consumer surplus was $85.42 per trip, and counterfactual welfare calculations indicate that keeping daily chl-a below the threshold would have increased total angling trips and raised annual surplus from $10.1 million to $16.2 million, implying a welfare loss of $6.0 million in 2022. The workflow illustrates how monitored biophysical indicators can be recast as threshold-triggered, stakeholder-relevant outcome metrics to support risk communication and adaptive management.

title: Asymmetric Multipolarity: Financial, Industrial, Resource, and Strategic Power in the Post-Unipolar Global Order
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Asymmetric Multipolarity: Financial, Industrial, Resource, and Strategic Power in the Post-Unipolar Global Order
detail.abstract: For three decades following the Cold War, international relations were characterized by a unipolar structure centered on Western financial and military hegemony. However, economic and geopolitical data from the early 21st century indicates a divergence between financial centrality and real-economy capacity. While popular narratives often frame this transition as a binary decline of the West and rise of the BRICS bloc, such models overlook the nuanced decoupling of power layers. This paper argues that the global system is not witnessing a simple replacement of hegemony, but a structural rebalancing across four distinct layers: financial (USD-dominant), industrial (Global South-leaning), resource (distributed), and strategic (military/logistics). Crucially, this multipolarity is asymmetric both within and across blocs meaning that leverage, dependency, and vulnerability are unevenly distributed across functions (e.g., financial centrality vs. industrial capacity) and actors (e.g., India vs. China within the Global South). By analyzing data on purchasing power parity, debt structures, critical mineral supply chains, digital infrastructure, and institutional competition particularly after the 2008 global financial crisis and the 2022 financial sanctions regime against Russia this study proposes a model of "Asymmetric Multipolarity." The findings suggest a transition not toward a new hegemon, but toward a fragmented system of competitive interdependence, where financial power no longer guarantees industrial or resource control. The paper concludes with layered policy implications and scenario modeling for 2025–2040, emphasizing that outcomes remain contingent on policy choices rather than deterministic trends.

title: IMPACT OF ECONOMIC SHOCKS ON CROSS-BORDER STRATEGIES: A BIBLIOMETRIC-SYSTEMATIC REVIEW

detail.title: IMPACT OF ECONOMIC SHOCKS ON CROSS-BORDER STRATEGIES: A BIBLIOMETRIC-SYSTEMATIC REVIEW
detail.abstract: Economic shocks affect both institutional and market conditions in home and host countries of a firm, putting pressures on its responses to organize and govern its cross-border operations. However,the lack of a holistic perspective has led to fragmented research on economic shocks and cross-border strategies, making it difficult to develop a coherent understanding of the mixed findings across heterogeneous contexts. This study examines how economic shocks shape firms’ cross-border strategies, focusing on changes in the timing of market entry and exit, relocation decision, ownership structure and performance outcomes. Our bibliometric-systematic review of studies revealed heterogeneity among three cross-border strategies, namely foreign direct investment, cross-border acquisitions and cross-border alliances. Based on this integrated review, we identify key research gaps and outline directions for future research.

title: From Buffer to Liability: Climate Risk, Financial Policy, and Bank Stability Across Emerging Market Economies
affiliations: University of KwaZulu-Natal, University of KwaZulu-Natal, Sunyani Technical University and University of the Free State

detail.title: From Buffer to Liability: Climate Risk, Financial Policy, and Bank Stability Across Emerging Market Economies
detail.abstract: We examine the effects of acute physical risk, chronic physical risk, and transition risk on bank stability and lending behaviour across 35 emerging market economies (EMEs) over 2000–2023, providing the first systematic cross-country panel study of the climate risk–banking nexus for the broader EME universe. Employing two-way fixed effects estimation with Driscoll-Kraay standard errors, we generate five principal findings. First, acute physical risk significantly destabilises upper-middle-income EME banking systems (β = -0.021, p < 0.05) but is insignificant in the full sample, reflecting income-differentiated transmission through financial integration and credit chain complexity. Second, transition risk operates as a short-run stability buffer in carbon-intensive EMEs (β = 7.101, p < 0.05, excluding crisis years), attenuated by stronger regulatory quality (β = -5.975, p < 0.01), consistent with the climate Minsky moment framework. Third, the CRFPI × transition risk interaction (β = 53.404, p < 0.001) provides the first cross-country panel evidence that comprehensive climate financial policy frameworks generate direct, large stability benefits for EME banking sectors. Fourth, governance quality fully mediates the climate risk–stability relationship in Africa and the MENA region (β = 9.498, p < 0.001), while regulatory quality is the dominant driver in lower-middle-income EMEs (β = 1.154, p < 0.05), confirming that institutional capacity is the primary resilience determinant in shallower financial systems. Fifth, the transition risk coefficient reverses sign from strongly positive in low-CRFPI countries (β = +6.978, p < 0.001) to significantly negative in high-CRFPI countries (β = -30.617, p < 0.01), confirming that policy-active banking systems have already internalised transition risk as a financial liability. These findings imply that differentiated climate financial regulation, calibrated to income group, institutional capacity, and carbon intensity, is essential for building climate-resilient banking systems across the heterogeneous EME universe.

title: Leakage-Free Multi-Site EV Charging Demand Forecasting: Cross-Site Generalization, Transfer Learning, and Grid-Aware Scheduling

detail.title: Leakage-Free Multi-Site EV Charging Demand Forecasting: Cross-Site Generalization, Transfer Learning, and Grid-Aware Scheduling

keywords: Keywords: Electric vehicle charging demand forecasting

detail.abstract: Precise short-term prediction of aggregate electric vehicle (EV) charging demand is robust in the areas of demand-side control, mitigation of the peak, and charging operations that are grid-aware. However, many published EV forecasting models cannot be compared or replicated, because of the utilization of single-site data, extra covariates or evaluation strategies that do not sustain time-varying sequence. A leakage-free time-aware forecasting model of the demand in a multi-site EV charging is suggested in this study on the basis of the ACN-Caltech data. The session level charge data of six charging stations are transformed into continuous hourly series of demand and all the models are trained by using only lagged historical demand characteristics, omitting calendar, weather, traffic, and price characteristics. Linear Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost are assessed by such controlled environment with the strict chronological order of training, validation, and testing. Gradient-boosting models are more effective than simple baselines in within-site forecasting in the reported experiments with LightGBM having the lowest MAE (12.41) and CatBoost having the lowest RMSE (17.96). The paper then makes a comparison of cross-site generalization of the heterogeneous locations in charging, and suggests that the direct transfer between locations makes less accurate predictions, which suggests the effect of distribution shift between sites. In this aspect, a transfer-learning setting is researched and fine-tuning on target-site information results in the intended performance (MAE 9.256 and RMSE 13.783). Finally, the predictions are used illustratively in an experiment on the redistribution of loads in the context of scheduling to demonstrate how increased prediction of demand can be helpful in improving the reduction of the peaks as well as smoothing the loads. The main importance of the work is that it offers a leakage-free, reproducible and deployment oriented benchmark of EV charging demand forecasting which interrelates within-site prediction, cross-site adaptation and downstream deployment operational application.

title: An Overlay Design Framework to Support Creativity in Prescriptive STM Curricula: A Case Study from a Moroccan Technical High School
affiliations: Hassan 2 University of Casablanca, Morocco, Hassan 2 University of Casablanca, Morocco, Hassan 2 University of Casablanca, Morocco and Hassan 2 University of Casablanca, Morocco

detail.title: An Overlay Design Framework to Support Creativity in Prescriptive STM Curricula: A Case Study from a Moroccan Technical High School
detail.abstract:
Developing engineers who can innovate under strict curricular requirements remains challenging in many African education systems. This study proposes and examines the Neural and Flexible Design Model, an iterative overlay framework designed to strengthen creativity without replacing mandatory engineering content in the Sciences et Technologies Mécaniques (STM) curriculum.
An embedded qualitative case study was conducted over 16 weeks with 34 first-year STM students (aged 16 to 17) in a Moroccan public technical high school, organised into four design teams as the unit of analysis. Each team designed a solution to improve the school environment and produced required deliverables, including functional analysis artifacts, prototyping, and computer-aided design (CAD) where relevant. Creative outcomes were assessed using a three-dimensional rubric covering cognitive and process quality, product quality, and psycho-social and value integration on a three-level ordinal scale (Expected, Original, Innovative). Findings were triangulated by an independent expert jury (n = 3) using five criteria: novelty, usefulness, feasibility, implementation quality, and systemic thinking.
Two projects were classified as Innovative and two as Original, indicating differentiated creative maturity under identical curricular constraints. Higher performance was associated with combining novelty with systemic integration and credible feasibility pathways, whereas novelty alone did not ensure feasibility or value integration. The findings suggest that the Neural and Flexible Design Model provides a pragmatic, reproducible overlay technique to support creative engineering problem-solving in constrained secondary technical education.

detail.abstract:
This project focuses on understanding how Crush Fitness India currently manages the process of assigning wellness professionals—such as fitness trainers, doctors, and mental health experts—to corporate clients, and where delays tend to occur within that process. As the organization follows an aggregator-based service model, it works with a wide network of freelance professionals spread across multiple cities. While this approach allows flexibility and rapid expansion, it also makes coordination and timely deployment more challenging. The study is based on a single-organization case study and closely examines the actual steps followed during the deployment cycle. Twenty-six recent service requests were reviewed in detail. For each request, time stamps were tracked from internal emails, CRM records, and WhatsApp communications to calculate how long each stage of the process took. In addition to this data, informal discussions with operations team members were conducted to better understand the practical reasons behind certain delays. 
The analysis clearly shows that the most time-consuming stage is the period spent waiting for service providers to confirm their availability. This sourcing and confirmation phase accounts for more than half of the total deployment time, making it the primary bottleneck in the workflow. Based on these findings, the project recommends practical and achievable improvements, such as pre-identifying preferred providers, setting clear response-time expectations, and improving visibility of provider availability. These changes are expected to reduce overall lead time and make the deployment process more reliable and easier to scale.

title: Augmenting Expert Knowledge: Modeling Bus Dispatcher Deadheading Decisions with Explainable Machine Learning
affiliations: Tongji University, Tongji University, Tongji University, Tongji University and Tongji University

detail.title: Augmenting Expert Knowledge: Modeling Bus Dispatcher Deadheading Decisions with Explainable Machine Learning
detail.abstract: Urban transit systems face a fundamental paradox during peak hours: passenger demand reaches its highest levels precisely when road congestion most severely impedes bus operations. To break this cycle, transit agencies employ deadheading—a control strategy where empty buses bypass intermediate stops to rapidly reposition fleet. Despite extensive research on optimal deadheading policies, little is known about how experienced dispatchers actually make these decisions in practice. This study proposes an expert-informed, four-stage framework—combining empirical foundation, predictive modeling, explainable machine learning interpretation, and model-human divergence assessment—to unravel real-world deadheading decision-making. Applying this framework to 42,480 bus trip records from a major Shanghai route over two years, we identify the key variables driving dispatcher choices through interviews and tree-based models (CART and GBDT). The proposed GBDT model achieves a 39.4% F1 improvement over naive heuristic rules (0.736 versus 0.528, p<0.001), with out-of-time and cross-weather validation confirming temporal and environmental robustness. Explainable machine learning analysis reveals that the deviation between actual and scheduled departure time, together with the minimum of forward and backward headways, are the most influential determinants. Model-human divergence analysis further shows that unobserved contextual factors—including tidal travel flows, anticipated delays, and end-of-shift considerations—explain residual model divergence, underscoring the value of maintaining human oversight. These findings provide empirical foundations for designing decision support systems that augment, rather than override, dispatcher expertise.

title:
MIO: A Conceptual Framework for Structured Self-Regulation under Conditions of Cognitive-Emotional Overload
An Analytical and Non-Therapeutic Approach to Regulation without Pathologization

MIO: A Conceptual Framework for Structured Self-Regulation under Conditions of Cognitive-Emotional Overload
An Analytical and Non-Therapeutic Approach to Regulation without Pathologization
